summary: Researchers at the Keck School of Medicine of USC have developed an AI model to fill gaps in brain wiring maps created with diffusion MRI. This technology may help researchers study how key brain connections change with aging and disease.

title: US stocks jump as Democrats win Senate and House, dollar falls
content:
US investors reacted positively to the results of the midterm elections, pushing the country’s major equity indexes higher.  The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed close to 3%, its best day in more than a year, while the Nasdaq and S&P 500 each gained about 1.5% by the close on Wednesday afternoon.  

The rally followed a shift in sentiment that eased early concerns about how the election outcome might affect growth in the world’s largest economy.  Market participants expressed hope that Donald Trump’s turbulent policymaking would be restrained under a new Democratic majority in both chambers of Congress.  

At the same time, U.S. government bond yields fell, and the gains in the stock market reversed overnight declines in U.S. futures that had emerged after the news that Democrats had secured control of the Senate and the House of Representatives.
summary: US stocks surged on Wednesday, with the Dow Jones up close to 3% and the Nasdaq and S&P 500 each gaining about 1.5% after Democrats secured control of the Senate and the House. Government bond yields fell and the dollar slid as investors eased concerns about the election’s impact on the economy.

content: Male hawkmoths utilize their genital structures as defensive tools by rubbing specialized scales against their abdomen. This action produces ultrasonic sounds that can disrupt the acoustic signals bats employ for hunting, providing the nocturnal insects with a survival advantage.

title: Geolinking Service SoRa strengthens interdisciplinary research in Germany
content:
The "Geolinking Service SoRa" research data infrastructure addresses a gap in the German research landscape by facilitating interdisciplinary analyses. This service enables the linking of social science and spatial science data, which is necessary to answer complex questions regarding social inequality and environmental justice.

Specific research inquiries supported by this infrastructure include determining if the proportion of green space in residential neighborhoods affects health and well-being. It also allows researchers to examine whether people living in single-family homes report higher happiness levels than those in densely built-up urban areas, and how transportation infrastructure, such as access to buses and trains, influences mobility patterns.
summary: The Geolinking Service SoRa research data infrastructure helps close a gap in the German research landscape by linking social science and spatial science data. This service enables interdisciplinary analyses of questions regarding social inequality, environmental justice, and the impact of neighborhood characteristics on health and mobility.

title: Review in Nature Reviews Biodiversity outlines light pollution's ecological impacts
content:
A recent review article published in Nature Reviews Biodiversity examines the ecological consequences of artificial nighttime lighting. The study, which included participation from the Leibniz Institute of Freshwater Ecology and Inland Fisheries (IGB), identifies light pollution as one of the fastest-growing and least-regulated environmental changes worldwide. The authors note that this phenomenon disrupts biological processes at all levels, ranging from genes to entire ecosystems, and contributes significantly to global biodiversity loss.

Based on a comprehensive assessment of impacts on organisms in both terrestrial and aquatic environments, the article outlines specific priorities for future research and management. The review aims to address the widespread effects of light pollution on biological systems, providing a framework for understanding its role in environmental degradation.
summary: A review article published in Nature Reviews Biodiversity assesses how artificial nighttime lighting disrupts biological processes and contributes to biodiversity loss. The study, which included participation from the Leibniz Institute of Freshwater Ecology and Inland Fisheries, identifies priorities for future research and management.

title: Research finds chiral topological phases in metals without structural order
content: New research has identified chiral topological phases in metals that lack structural order. Fermions, which include everyday electrons and exotic variants, are fundamental particles in physics. Chiral fermions, first proposed over a century ago, exist in left- and right-handed versions, analogous to gloves. Although high-energy neutrinos were initially considered leading candidates for massless chiral fermions, they were found to possess mass. Instead, nearly semi-metallic solid-state crystals were discovered fifteen years ago to host electronic versions of these massless chiral fermions.
summary: New research has uncovered chiral topological phases in metals that lack structural order. Nearly semi-metallic solid-state crystals were found 15 years ago to host electronic versions of massless chiral fermions.

title: Toothbrush that emits electricity may more effectively prevent gum disease
content:
A novel toothbrush utilizing piezoelectric bristles has demonstrated superior efficacy in reducing dental plaque and gum inflammation compared to conventional products. Developed by researchers led by Yanhui Lu at Peking University in China, the device generates electricity as its bristles bend during brushing. This mechanical action triggers the formation of reactive-oxygen species, molecules that damage bacterial membranes, while the bristles simultaneously remove plaque physically. The innovation addresses the limitation of standard brushing, which often leaves bacteria deep within plaque or between teeth, allowing colonies to regrow rapidly.

The research team created two sets of bristles with varying thicknesses, both of which adhered to Chinese national standards for softness and strength. Laboratory tests confirmed that the bristles produced electric charges under pressure, with the thicker variants showing particularly high electrical generation. The brushes retained their softness and electrical properties after three months of use. In controlled experiments involving simulated brushing movements, the thicker piezoelectric bristles killed approximately 53 per cent of Streptococcus mutans, a bacterium associated with cavities, and 78 per cent of Porphyromonas gingivalis, which contributes to gum disease. In contrast, standard nylon bristles eliminated only 9 per cent and 8 per cent of these bacteria, respectively.

Further testing involved growing plaque from human mouths on cow enamel pieces and brushing them for three minutes. The piezoelectric toothbrushes removed more than 99 per cent of the plaque, whereas conventional nylon brushes removed about 80 per cent. The study also included a clinical trial with 109 adults who had dental plaque and gum inflammation. Participants were randomly assigned to use either the piezoelectric or a nylon toothbrush twice daily for three months. Dental examinations showed that the piezoelectric group experienced reductions of roughly 40 per cent in plaque build-up, gum inflammation, and bleeding, compared to around 15 per cent for the conventional brush group.

Genetic sequencing of dental plaque from the piezoelectric user group indicated a decline in the relative abundance of harmful bacteria and an increase in some potentially beneficial bacteria. Nicholas Jakubovics, a researcher at Newcastle University in the UK who was not involved in the study, described the concept as innovative because the mechanical forces recharge the surface. He noted that any improvement in dental care methods could be beneficial given the widespread nature of oral disease, which affects nearly half the global population. Previous attempts to enhance toothbrushes have included antibacterial metal nanoparticles or battery-dependent ionic currents, but the long-term effectiveness of some of these methods remains uncertain.

The findings were published in the journal Science Advances. Jakubovics emphasized that larger studies are now required to determine whether the toothbrush effectively prevents long-term issues such as cavities and tooth loss. The research highlights a potential advancement in oral hygiene tools by leveraging piezoelectric materials, which have previously been shown to fight bacteria in infected wounds and medical implants.
summary: A new and improved toothbrush could help avoid trips to the dentist Westend61/Alamy A toothbrush that generates electricity may more effectively fight harmful bacteria, while removing plaque, than existing products. The toothbrush uses special bristles that produce electricity as they bend, triggering the formation of molecules that damage bacterial membranes.

title: Hubble Study Finds Dwarf Galaxies Retain Only Small Fraction of Stellar Oxygen
content:
NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope has captured a new image of NGC 4449, a dwarf irregular galaxy featured in the Galaxies Losing Oxygen via Winds (GLOW) study. Released on November 2, 2026, the photograph highlights this specific galaxy as part of a broader investigation into stellar oxygen retention.

Researchers utilized Hubble to examine 37 nearby dwarf galaxies, defined as small systems containing thousands to hundreds of millions of stars. The study revealed that these galaxies retain only a small fraction of the oxygen produced by their stars, leaving much of the expected oxygen missing. This finding underscores a significant cosmic mystery regarding how dwarf galaxies manage their elemental composition.
summary: Researchers using NASA's Hubble Space Telescope studied 37 nearby dwarf galaxies and found that much of the expected oxygen is missing. The study, known as GLOW, revealed that these small galaxies can hold onto only a small fraction of the oxygen made by their stars.
author: NASA News

title: NASA awards Ka-band satellite relay contracts to Astranis, Global Enterprise, Viasat
content:
NASA announced on Wednesday that it has awarded contracts to three companies to develop Ka‑band space relay capability concepts that are compatible with current missions in space. The selected firms will design solutions that maintain service continuity for existing spacecraft without requiring modifications to their onboard systems. The work is intended to deliver end‑to‑end solutions—including space, ground, launch, operations, and integration elements—as part of NASA’s broader commercial marketplace strategy.

The awards are firm‑fixed‑price contracts issued under the Next Space Technologies for Exploration Partnerships‑3 Broad Agency Announcement Appendix E. NASA retains the option to provide additional funding, up to the award limit, to advance the projects from initial concept development and risk reduction to an in‑orbit flight demonstration. The initial period of performance runs from November 4 through May 3, 2027, with priced options that could extend the work through 2029.

The contract awardees and their maximum potential values, inclusive of all future options, are: Astranis Space Technologies Corp. for $264.3 million; Global Enterprise Solutions Inc. for $340.4 million; and Viasat Inc. for $460.9 million. These contracts are facilitated through NASA’s SCaN (Space Communications and Navigation) program’s Communications Services Project.

The work supports NASA’s decision to gradually retire the Tracking and Data Relay Satellite fleet and adopt commercial services for future missions. Ka‑band services are also required to support select in‑orbit missions that cannot feasibly modify flight hardware or transition to non‑compatible commercial services. For additional information, visit https://go.Nasa.gov/4iVfeVB.
summary: NASA awards Ka-band satellite relay contracts to Astranis, Global Enterprise, Viasat.
author: NASA News

title: ChatGPT can now create animated GIFs from prompts or photos
content:

The update, released alongside the Images 2.6 model, also provides tools to adjust the GIF’s playback speed, edit individual frames, and share the finished file with others.

Previously, ChatGPT could not natively produce GIFs. In a demonstration, the AI responded to the prompt “can you make a gif of a cat dancing?” by generating the animation and offering options to change the speed and view each frame. The Images 2.6 update expands the platform’s image‑generation capabilities beyond static pictures.

title: AT&T Connects Gemini for Home to Its Smart Security System
content:
AT&T has announced that its Connected Life smart home security system is the first product to integrate with Google Home Premium. This partnership enables users to access a range of Gemini-powered features within their security ecosystem.

The update allows Gemini for Home to provide detailed descriptions of events captured by security cameras, such as identifying package delivery personnel and counting dropped items. Users can also search recorded video footage using natural language queries, with examples including "What dug up the yard last night?" or "Who let the dogs out?"
summary: AT&T’s Connected Life smart home security system now integrates with Gemini for Home, making it the first home security product to work with Google Home Premium. The update allows detailed descriptions of camera events and natural‑language searches of recorded footage.
author: The Verge

title: Bose QuietComfort Headphones Over Half Off at Amazon, Best Buy, Bose
content:
Bose’s QuietComfort headphones are currently available at steep discounts across major retailers. The first‑generation QuietComfort Headphones are on sale for $169.99, a $190 markdown from their original $359 price, on Amazon, Best Buy, and Bose’s own website. The newer second‑generation QuietComfort Headphones, launched in August, are discounted to $199, a $160 reduction from $359, and are available in multiple colors on the same platforms. The second‑gen price is only $20 above Bose’s all‑time low.

Both models retain Bose’s reputation for effective noise cancellation, clear sound, and a 24‑hour battery life. The original QuietComfort Headphones support multipoint Bluetooth connectivity, allowing simultaneous connections to two devices, and feature a lightweight, foldable design that eases portability.

The second‑generation QuietComfort Headphones build on the first‑gen foundation with several upgrades. They support lossless audio via USB‑C and include a three‑band equalizer in Bose’s companion app, which reviewers have used to adjust vocal levels. According to reviewer John Higgins, the default sound profile of the second‑gen QuietComfort Headphones is the best he has heard from Bose, surpassing even the flagship QuietComfort Ultra Gen 2. Higgins also noted that the second‑gen headphones feel more comfortable than the Ultra, lacking the “eardrum suck” sensation caused by strong active noise cancellation.

Consumers looking for high‑quality noise‑canceling headphones can take advantage of these discounts, with the first‑gen offering a budget option and the second‑gen providing modest upgrades for a modest additional cost.
summary: The first‑generation Bose QuietComfort Headphones are on sale for $169.99, $190 off, at Amazon, Best Buy, and Bose. The second‑generation version, launched in August, is discounted to $199, $160 off, and features upgrades such as lossless audio via USB‑C and a better default sound profile.
author: The Verge

title: Laura Bohn discovers opioid alternative SR‑17018 that avoids respiratory depression
content:
Laura Bohn, senior associate vice president of research at University of South Florida Health, was tasked in 2012 with finding safer pain‑management drugs as the opioid crisis shifted from prescription pills to heroin. The National Institute on Drug Abuse funded her work.

In 2017 Bohn and colleagues published in the journal Cell that several compounds, including a promising one named SR‑17018, could relieve pain in mice without causing respiratory depression—a common cause of opioid‑related death. The study highlighted SR‑17018’s potential to reduce pain without the life‑threatening breathing suppression seen with many opioids.

The team filed a patent on SR‑17018 and discovered that mice treated with the chemical did not develop a high tolerance. Additionally, mice already dependent on morphine could consume SR‑17018 to reset their tolerance without experiencing painful withdrawal symptoms.
summary: Laura Bohn discovers opioid alternative SR‑17018 that avoids respiratory depression.
author: Ars Technica

title: Slate Auto's Electric Truck Prototype Receives Positive 45-Minute Test Drive
content:
A 45‑minute drive from southwest Washington, D.C. to Rockville, Maryland, gave the author a firsthand look at Slate Auto’s electric truck prototype. The company invited the author to test the vehicle without the need for a flight or overnight hotel stay, making the experience straightforward and accessible.

The prototype had accumulated almost 6,000 miles (9,656 km) as shown on its small, minimalist digital display. That display also shows the vehicle’s speed and, when the driver engages reverse, the backup camera feed. While the cabin layout mirrors what the production version will look like, the interior surfaces differ: the prototype uses hard, shiny black plastic and retains strips of Velcro that were left over from earlier public test runs.

The door handles resemble those on a Morris Marina, operating with a pleasing mechanical action. Both the seat and steering column adjust manually and offer ample reach, a feature that many budget models often omit to cut costs.
summary: Slate Auto's prototype electric truck was driven for 45 minutes, covering almost 6,000 miles, and featured a minimalist digital display showing speed and backup camera when reverse is engaged. The cabin layout was representative of the production version, with manual seat and steering column adjustments and door handles that open with a pleasing mechanical action.
author: Ars Technica

title: Binance says hackers who stole billions in crypto spent months planning heist
content:
Binance announced that a group of hackers, identified by the FBI and TRM Security as North Korean actors, carried out a theft that targeted $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency from its wallets. The attackers used social‑engineering tactics and novel malware, and the operation began no later than June, continuing until last Thursday when they successfully compromised an engineer’s laptop and withdrew assets from several wallets.

The exchange reports that it has frozen or intercepted $2.85 billion of the stolen amount. Binance has set aside the funds necessary to cover the loss and has linked to a Proof of Reserves page to demonstrate its financial position. The $6.34 billion figure represents the largest sum ever targeted in a cryptocurrency theft.

Binance described the threat actors as sophisticated and resourceful, noting that the heist was the result of months of planning and execution.
summary: Binance says hackers who stole billions in crypto spent months planning heist.
author: Ars Technica

title: Enough Phone launches 5.3‑inch smartphone with removable battery
content:
The Enough Phone company has announced that it will begin taking pre‑orders for its first device today, targeting consumers who have expressed a desire for smaller smartphones. The handset features a 5.3‑inch HD+ LCD display, which the company claims is the smallest screen it could find that still offers acceptable performance.

In terms of hardware, the Enough Phone is powered by a MediaTek Dimensity 7500 system‑on‑chip, paired with 8 GB of RAM and 128 GB of internal storage, expandable via microSD. The rear camera is a single Sony IMX766 50‑megapixel sensor, while the front camera is 32 MP. The phone runs Android 17 or OdysseyOS, has a removable 3,500‑mAh battery, and supports 5G, LTE, Wi‑Fi 6, Bluetooth, NFC, and dual SIM (SIM + eSIM). Its polycarbonate body houses a fingerprint sensor integrated into the power button.

The device measures 133 × 64 × 12 mm and is priced at $399 for a limited‑time offer, with a $599 MSRP thereafter. The design, while slightly thicker than many competitors, is comparable in footprint to the iPhone 13 Mini and allows users to replace the battery by removing a few screws, similar to the Fairphone.
summary: Enough Phone has begun taking preorders for its first device, a 5.3‑inch smartphone with a removable battery and a MediaTek Dimensity 7500 SoC. The phone comes with 8 GB RAM, 128 GB storage, a 50 MP Sony rear camera, 3500 mAh battery, and is priced at $399 for a limited time or $599 MSRP.
author: Ars Technica

title: Sequoia consolidates, closes 20-year expansion offices, announces $10B in new funds
content: Sequoia is consolidating its operations into a smaller, Bay‑Area‑centered firm, closing the programs and offices created during a 20‑year expansion. At the same time, the firm announced the launch of new funds totaling roughly $10 billion.
summary: Sequoia is consolidating into a smaller, Bay Area–centered firm and shutting down the programs and offices it built during a 20‑year expansion. The firm also announced roughly $10 billion in new funds.
author: TechCrunch

title: Hugging Face discusses profit opportunities as open source AI booms
content: The episode discusses how open‑source AI models are moving into mainstream use by enterprises, governments and startups because they promise lower costs, greater control and flexibility. It examines how companies can capture value as increasingly capable models become freely available and considers whether American firms can keep pace with the rise of Chinese open‑source models.
summary: Open source AI models are becoming more mainstream as enterprises, governments and startups adopt them for lower costs, greater control and flexibility. Hugging Face explains how companies can capture value and whether American firms can keep pace with rising Chinese open models.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI’s Chris Lehane proposes AI-driven social contract for 2028 election
content: OpenAI executive Chris Lehane says he wants artificial intelligence to define the 2028 election, proposing a new social contract that he says could benefit Americans while also advancing OpenAI’s business interests.
summary: OpenAI’s Chris Lehane says AI should define the 2028 election. He proposes a new social contract that could benefit Americans while also advancing OpenAI’s business interests.
author: TechCrunch

title: Pilates and yoga studios across US urged followers to vote in midterm elections
content: Owners of pilates and yoga studios in the US got political and encouraged their followers to vote on social media Your local pilates instructors only want you to do two things: breathe through your side-planks and vote. In the days leading up to the US midterm elections, a wave of posts from fitness and wellness accounts blanketed Instagram, eschewing their typical messaging around the importance of strengthening your core in favor of the importance of exercising your civic duty. Owners of pilates and yoga studios and instructors across the US posted reels and pictures on platforms like Instagram encouraging their followers and clients to vote. Engagement varied depending on their following: posts reaped anywhere from 70 to more than 10,000 likes.
summary: Owners of Pilates and yoga studios in the US posted Instagram reels and pictures encouraging their followers and clients to vote in the midterm elections. The posts garnered engagement ranging from about 70 likes to more than 10,000 likes.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Trump says rising petrol prices from Iran war hurt GOP, praises Democrats after midterms
content: US President Donald Trump has acknowledged that rising petrol prices linked to the war in Iran contributed to his Republican Party's defeat in the midterm elections. He said voters supported his actions against Iran but were reluctant to pay more at the pump. Trump also praised Democrats.
summary: President Donald Trump said rising petrol prices linked to the war in Iran helped cause the Republican Party’s loss in the midterm elections. He added that voters supported his actions against Iran but were reluctant to pay more at the pump, and he praised Democrats.
author: Euronews

title: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate seat, first Muslim in US Senate
content: Democrat Abdul El‑Sayed, a 42‑year‑old physician who identifies with the progressive wing of his party, won Michigan’s U.S. Senate race, defeating Republican Mike Rogers. His victory makes him the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, securing a seat that Republicans had hoped to flip.
summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has won Michigan's Senate race against Republican Mike Rogers, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. The 42-year-old physician, who represents the progressive wing of the Democratic Party, secured a seat that Republicans had hoped to flip.
author: Euronews

title: Young Portland voters celebrate Democratic sweep in 2026 midterms
content: Young voters in Portland, Maine, celebrated the Democrats’ sweeping victories in the 2026 midterm elections, with celebrations breaking out as results were announced. Several described the outcome as a “moment of redemption” after years of political disappointment.
summary: Young voters in Portland, Maine welcomed the Democrats' sweeping victories in the 2026 midterm elections, with celebrations breaking out as results came in. They described the outcome as a moment of redemption after years of political disappointment.
author: Euronews

title: Armenian PM Nikol Pashinyan says South Caucasus can play new global role via pro‑EU peace
content: Armenia’s Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan told Euronews that peace and convergence in the South Caucasus, based on a carefully balanced pro-EU political vector, create a major opportunity for the region, with "democracy as a strategy" for Armenia.
summary: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said Armenia sees a totally new global role for the South Caucasus as a whole. He told Euronews that peace and convergence in the region, based on a balanced pro‑EU political vector, create a major opportunity and that democracy is Armenia’s strategy.
author: Euronews

title: Police bodycam shows Russian bomb hitting Komyshuvakha shelter, 37 dead
content: Body‑cam footage from a police officer who was killed in the attack shows the moments just before a Russian bomb struck a shelter in Komyshuvakha, Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region. The strike killed at least 37 people.
summary: Bodycam footage from a police officer who was killed captured the moments before a Russian bomb struck a shelter in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region. The attack killed at least 37 people.
author: Euronews

title: Police arrest Palestine Action supporters outside London Supreme Court
content: Police arrested supporters of Palestine Action outside the Supreme Court in London on Wednesday, 4 November. The arrests occurred as a legal battle over the British government’s ban on the group resumed.
summary: Police arrested supporters of Palestine Action outside the Supreme Court in London on Wednesday 4 November. The arrests came as a legal battle over the British government’s ban on the group resumed.
author: Euronews

title: Santa Claus School graduates 55 Santas at Rio's Christ the Redeemer
content: Dozens of Santas gathered at Rio de Janeiro’s iconic Christ the Redeemer statue to mark the graduation of Santa Claus School. The ceremony welcomed 55 new recruits, who will now travel across Brazil to spread Christmas cheer.
summary: Dozens of Santas gathered at Rio de Janeiro's iconic Christ the Redeemer statue to celebrate their graduation. The 55 new recruits are preparing to spread Christmas cheer across Brazil.
author: Euronews

title: US Midterms: Trump faces challenge of cooperating with Democratic Congress
content:
Democrats are riding their sweep of Congress into a new era, eager to meet voter demands for change with plans to tackle high costs of living.  

How will Donald Trump manage to work with them? France 24's Ophelie Jacobson has more.
summary: Democrats have swept Congress and are pursuing plans to address high living costs. The piece asks how Donald Trump will manage to work with the newly empowered Democrats, with further analysis by France 24’s Ophelie Jacobson.
author: France 24

title: Schumer Discusses Midterm Results and Future Plans
content: Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer addressed the press following the midterm election results. He said Democrats are riding a sweep of Congress into a new era, emphasizing a desire to meet voter demands for change. Schumer highlighted plans to tackle high costs of living and to confront President Donald Trump’s final years in the White House.
summary: The US Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer talked to the press after the midterm election results. He said Democrats plan to tackle high costs of living and confront President Donald Trump's final years in the White House.
author: France 24

title: Iran's Deputy Parliament Speaker Ali Nikzad blames US war for Republican midterm losses
content: First Deputy Speaker of the Parliament of Iran Ali Nikzad on Wednesday attributed Republican losses in the US midterm elections to Washington's war with Iran, telling lawmakers that American efforts to pressure Tehran had failed. Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections.
summary: First Deputy Speaker of the Parliament of Iran Ali Nikzad said Republican losses in the US midterm elections were due to Washington's war with Iran. Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections.
author: France 24

title: US midterms yield historic firsts: minority senators and Georgia's first Black governor
content: The recent U.S. midterm elections produced several historic firsts: Minnesota elected its first Native American female senator, New Hampshire chose its first openly gay male senator, Michigan selected its first Muslim senator, and Georgia appointed the nation’s first Black female governor. France 24’s Elitsa Gadeva reports further details on these milestones.
summary: The US midterm elections produced a wave of historic firsts as minorities won key races. They include the first Native American female senator in Minnesota, the first openly gay male senator in New Hampshire, the first Muslim senator in Michigan, and the country's first Black female governor in Georgia.
author: France 24

title: European leaders hope for US reset after Democrats win midterms
content: European leaders said on Wednesday, November 4, that they hope for a reset in relations with the United States after voters handed President Donald Trump and his Republican Party a large defeat in the midterm elections. FRANCE 24’s Dave Keating reports the comments.
summary: European leaders voiced hopes for a reset with the United States on Wednesday, November 4. Voters delivered a huge midterm election defeat to President Donald Trump and his Republican party.
author: France 24

title: Democrats' sweeping midterm win called “once‑in‑a‑generation” repudiation of Trump
content:
Erin Ogunkeye welcomed Adam Jentleson, President of the Searchlight Institute and author of Supermajority: How Democrats Can Build Lasting Power, to discuss the recent midterm election.  

Jentleson said the Democrats’ sweeping victory is “more than the familiar backlash against an incumbent president.” He described it as a “once‑in‑a‑generation event” that signals a historic repudiation of Trump and the MAGA movement.  

The president noted that the electoral breadth of the win creates a governing dilemma. He asked whether a coalition that includes progressive reformers and culturally conservative Democrats can translate its diversity into legislative action. “Pluralism is not just a political strategy. It is actually a moral good in a democracy,” he insisted.  

Jentleson also questioned whether a party united by opposition to Trump can maintain that unity when faced with difficult choices on healthcare, immigration, economic inequality, and climate change.
summary: Adam Jentleson, president of the Searchlight Institute, said the Democrats' sweeping midterm victory is a once‑in‑a‑generation repudiation of Trump and the MAGA movement. He cautioned that the party’s broad coalition of progressive reformers and culturally conservative Democrats may struggle to turn its diversity into legislative action.
author: France 24

title: Democrats warn Trump camp to ‘lawyer up’ as anger over corruption drives midterms wipeout
content: Corruption in government was high on the minds of US voters as they dealt US President Donald Trump’s party a chastening defeat in midterm elections, toppling Republican strongholds like dominoes and flipping both chambers of Congress. Triumphant Democrats have warned the Trump administration to “lawyer up”; how they go about tackling alleged graft and abuse of power could shape both their own fortunes and the country’s politics.
summary: Democrats warn Trump camp to ‘lawyer up’ as anger over corruption drives midterms wipeout.
author: France 24

title: Midterm results show Democratic landslide as voters target Trump's Republican majorities
content: Voters across the United States responded to a request to imagine Donald Trump on the ballot, and according to the source they moved to displace Republican majorities in both chambers of Congress. The commentary frames the outcome as a possible Democratic landslide in the midterm elections.
summary: Voters across the United States chased Donald Trump's Republican majorities in both houses of Congress. The outcome was a landslide for the Democrats.
author: France 24

title: Wawira Njiru receives German Africa Prize for Kenyan school feeding scheme
content: Wawira Njiru’s school‑feeding programme in Kenya, which began as a modest fundraiser, has expanded into a major enterprise that exceeded her expectations. In recognition of this achievement, she is being awarded the German Africa Prize.
summary: Wawira Njiru's Kenyan school feeding scheme grew from a small fundraiser to a major enterprise. She is now being awarded the German Africa Prize.
author: DW World

title: Kosovo protests after Arlinda Zekaj's murder, authorities blamed for inaction
content: In Kosovo, thousands of demonstrators are protesting what they describe as a dramatic failure of state institutions after Arlinda Zekaj was brutally murdered. Zekaj had reported her husband to the police and pleaded for protection before the killing.
summary: Arlinda Zekaj reported her husband to the police and pleaded for protection before she was brutally murdered. Thousands in Kosovo are now protesting, saying state institutions failed to help the femicide victim.
author: DW World

title: Hungary releases Communist-era secret service files 36 years after Soviet rule
content: Hungary is releasing all of its Communist-era secret‑service files, a step taken 36 years after the end of Soviet rule. The disclosure is prompting renewed discussion about the role of informants and questions of guilt and responsibility.
summary: Hungary is releasing all of its Communist-era secret service files decades after the end of Soviet rule. The disclosure is sparking fresh debate about informants, guilt and responsibility.
author: DW World

title: Republicans suffer crushing defeat as Democrats take Congress in US midterms
content: Donald Trump’s Republican candidates experienced a crushing defeat in Tuesday’s midterm elections, while Democratic candidates secured control of Congress. The results signal a shift in congressional power from Republicans to Democrats, prompting questions about the implications for U.S. politics and international affairs.
summary: Donald Trump's Republican candidates suffered a crushing defeat in Tuesday's midterm elections. The Democrats gained control of Congress.
author: DW World

title: Midterms signal rebuke of US‑Israel ties as Trump proposes cutting aid
content: Even Trump seems to recognize that the relationship has become a political liability, and may never be the same On the eve of a midterm election that ended in an unequivocal rejection of his brand of politics, even Donald Trump seemed to recognize that the US-Israel relationship had become a political liability. Trump’s 11th-hour suggestion, on election morning, that he would cut military aid to Israel at the end of the year because, as he put it, “they don’t need it”, was condemned across the board – with pro-Palestinian advocates dismissing it as “desperate” and pro-Israel ones as “unserious”.
summary: Midterms signal rebuke of US‑Israel ties as Trump proposes cutting aid.
author: Guardian World

title: Spain high‑speed train crash kills 69, shatters rail confidence
content:
A high‑speed train operated by Spain’s state‑owned rail company Renfe collided with the rear of a stationary train run by private operator Iryo at 8:53 a.m. on Wednesday near the town of Urda in Castilla‑La Mancha. The crash killed 69 people and injured more than 100, further eroding public confidence in the country’s rail network.

Pedro Sánchez and his socialist‑led coalition government are now racing to rebuild that confidence ahead of a snap election, a task described as immense. The recent accident adds to a pattern of deadly train crashes that have already left Spain’s rail system’s reputation depleted.
summary: Spain high‑speed train crash kills 69, shatters rail confidence.
author: Guardian World

title: Italian director Tinto Brass, known for Caligula, dies at 93
content:
Italian film director Tinto Brass, who began his career as an assistant to Roberto Rossellini, died at the age of 93.  

He moved into sex films, believing “eroticism to be a fundamental key to human expression” and was known as a maestro of Euro erotica.  

Brass was once hailed as the “Antonioni of the 70s” and became known for bringing Italian erotic cinema to a wider audience with films such as Caligula and Salon Kitty.  

His wife Caterina Varzi and children Bonifacio and Beatrice Brass announced the news to the Italian press agency Ansa on Wednesday.
summary: Tinto Brass, an Italian film director famous for erotic movies such as Caligula and Salon Kitty, died at age 93. His wife Caterina Varzi and children Bonifacio and Beatrice Brass announced his death to the Italian press agency Ansa on Wednesday.
author: Guardian World

title: Serbia detains nine police officers and one former officer over alleged force on protesters
content:
Serbian authorities detained ten police officers – nine active and one former – on Wednesday, accusing them of using excessive force against detainees during anti‑corruption protests in Belgrade last year, the interior ministry said. The ministry added that the suspects allegedly tortured and intimidated protesters who were held in a garage of a government compound.

The protests, which swept Serbia, an EU membership candidate, in 2025 and 2026, followed a 1 November 2024 incident in Novi Sad where a concrete canopy collapsed at a renovated railway station, killing 16 people.
summary: Serbia detains nine police officers and one former officer over alleged force on protesters.
author: Guardian World

title: Organic dates from illegal West Bank settlements shipped to Australia as ‘produce of Israel’
content: Analysis by human rights organisation Global Echo shows 85 of 132 shipments over eight years contained more than US$5m of organic dates grown in settlements Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Millions of dollars of food grown in illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank has been shipped to Australia labelled as “produce of Israel”, new analysis of trade data has shown. Human rights legal organisation Global Echo has analysed commercial documents and official trade data from the Israeli government and the Australian Bureau of Statistics, showing at least US$5m (A$7.2m) of organic dates grown in illegal settlements across the West Bank have been shipped to Australia over the past eight years.
summary: Organic dates from illegal West Bank settlements shipped to Australia as ‘produce of Israel’.
author: Guardian World

title: Telstra apologises for phantom missed call notifications caused by MessageBank issue
content: Telstra has issued an apology after thousands of its customers reported receiving phantom missed‑call notifications and voicemails, some appearing days after the call. The telecom said the problem stemmed from its MessageBank service. Telstra confirmed that the issue was identified on Wednesday night and that the service was restored later that same day. The company acknowledged the confusion caused to users and affirmed that the fault has been fixed.
summary: Thousands of Telstra users reported phantom calls, receiving delayed missed‑call notifications or voicemails sometimes days later. Telstra said the problem stemmed from its MessageBank service, apologized and confirmed the issue was fixed on Wednesday night.
author: Guardian World

title: Two women killed near home in British Columbia in suspected multi‑bear grizzly attack
content:
Conservation officers in British Columbia have confirmed that a 20-year-old woman and her mother were killed in an attack near their home. Search teams located the women’s bodies late Tuesday near a trail a short distance from their residence. The pair had been reported missing over the weekend.

Authorities stated that more than one grizzly bear may have been involved in the incident.
summary: Conservation officers in British Columbia said a 20‑year‑old woman and her mother were found dead near a trail a short distance from their home after being reported missing over the weekend. Officers now believe the fatal grizzly bear attack may have involved more than one bear.
author: Guardian World

title: British healthcare worker with Ebola evacuated from DRC to UK
content:
A British healthcare worker who tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is being evacuated to the United Kingdom for treatment. The patient is in stable condition and will be transferred to a specialist “high consequence” infectious disease unit upon arrival.

A UK government spokesperson confirmed the case, noting that established procedures for such situations have been activated and that the risk to the UK public remains low.
summary: British healthcare worker with Ebola evacuated from DRC to UK.
author: Guardian World

title: Ramayana: Rise of a Legend Review: Nitesh Tiwari’s Epic Stars Ranbir Kapoor
content:
Nitesh Tiwari’s three-hour film, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, is described as India’s most expensive production to date and the first half of a larger epic. The movie adapts the ancient classical poem concerning Rama, the avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu, into a spectacular Indian melodrama featuring music by Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman. While the story has been adapted for screen in the past, this version is noted for its unprecedented scale and lacks musical numbers.

The narrative follows Rama, portrayed by Ranbir Kapoor, as a noble warrior and statesman in the city-state of Ayodhya. His destiny involves confronting Ravana, played by Naveen “Yash” Kumar, the king of Lanka. The source details that Ravana’s backstory includes a period of slavery that led him to pray for justice, resulting in Lord Brahma granting him superhuman athletic strength and indifference to pain. The film is characterized as a thoroughly engaging and rousing blockbuster that appeals to audiences seeking a grand, Shakespearean-style tale of duty and war.
summary: The three-hour film directed by Nitesh Tiwari features music by Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman. Ranbir Kapoor plays Rama in this first-half blockbuster based on the ancient classical poem.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Review: Amazon's The Greatest retells Muhammad Ali's well-known life
content:
Amazon’s new limited series, The Greatest, offers a straightforward retelling of Muhammad Ali’s life, aiming to introduce the boxing icon to younger generations. The Prime Video drama is described as the first-ever “authorized scripted series” about Ali and features his widow, Lonnie, as an executive producer. While the show claims to be based on Ali’s life, it primarily takes its direction from a definitive book authored by his younger brother, Rahaman Ali.

Rahaman Ali, who served as a lifelong sparring partner and prominent member of the champion’s entourage until his death in 2016, provides the narrative foundation for the adaptation. The series covers well-known aspects of Ali’s biography, including his rise in boxing, his exile from the sport for refusing the draft, his late-career comeback, and his resilience following a Parkinson’s diagnosis.

Critics note that while the show offers small pleasures, it lacks novelty for most viewers. The review suggests that the adaptation repackages a story told too many times, reflecting a viewing public with diminishing patience for source material. The series is characterized as sturdy but ultimately unoriginal, relying on the cultural ubiquity of Ali’s public figure status to justify its existence.
summary: The Amazon Prime Video limited series The Greatest repackages Muhammad Ali's life, drawing heavily on the definitive book by his brother Rahaman Ali. The show serves as the first authorized scripted series about the boxer and features his widow Lonnie as an executive producer.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Patrick Stewart remembered by readers for RSC roles and community support
content: From coaching youth community theatre to supporting Huddersfield football club and delighting sci-fi fans at graduation ceremonies, the actor is fondly remembered Patrick Stewart – a life in pictures On Star Trek, Patrick Stewart could make anyone feel hopeful for humanity Patrick Stewart brought gravitas and complexity to the screen ‘He stood for the best of us’: William Shatner and more pay tribute What I always loved about Patrick was that he genuinely seemed connected to where he came from despite his global success. Once a Yorkshireman, always a Yorkshireman. I was lucky enough to see him at the Royal Shakespeare Company performing Hamlet, Merchant of Venice, and in Godot at the Haymarket, which is the only time the play has been so brilliantly performed as to make sense to me. I loved that he supported causes he clearly believed in, such as tackling domestic violence. He remained a good old-fashioned socialist. Got to applaud that. Shirley, 55, West Yorkshire
summary: Readers recall Patrick Stewart's performances in Royal Shakespeare Company productions such as Hamlet and Waiting for Godot. They also highlight his support for local causes, including Huddersfield football club and efforts to tackle domestic violence.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Celebrities react to Democrats' historic 2026 midterms sweep
content: After the party regained control of both houses of Congress, stars including Viola Davis, Bette Midler and John Cusack have been celebrating US midterms 2026 live – latest updates Track live results from all 50 states Tell us: what do you want to know about midterm results? Celebrities have been reacting to last night’s historic midterm victory for the Democrats after the party regained control of both the House and the Senate. The night saw a string of major victories for the party as voters expressed their disapproval of Donald Trump and his failing economy.
summary: Stars including Viola Davis, Bette Midler, and John Cusack celebrated the Democratic Party's victory in the 2026 US midterms. The party regained control of both the House and the Senate, with voters expressing disapproval of Donald Trump and his failing economy.
author: Guardian Culture

title: FSG in talks to buy majority stake in Cadillac F1 for over £2bn
content:
Liverpool owner Fenway Sports Group has held talks regarding the acquisition of a majority stake in the Cadillac Formula One team. The proposed deal is valued at more than £2bn and comes as Mark Walter continues to divest his sporting assets amid allegations of insurance fraud.

Cadillac entered Formula One this year as a joint venture between General Motors and Walter’s TWG Global. TWG Global recently sold its controlling interest in the NBA’s Los Angeles Lakers and a 13% stake in Chelsea, and is currently exploring the sale of the WNBA’s Los Angeles Sparks.
summary: Fenway Sports Group has held talks to acquire a majority stake in the Cadillac Formula One team for more than £2bn. The potential deal is part of Mark Walter's ongoing sale of sporting assets, including his controlling interest in the Los Angeles Lakers and a 13% stake in Chelsea.
author: Guardian Sport

title: West Ham appoint Scott Parker as head coach after sacking Nuno Espírito Santo
content:
West Ham United announced that former midfielder Scott Parker will become the club’s head coach following the dismissal of Nuno Espírito Santo on Tuesday. Parker signed a two‑and‑a‑half‑year contract and will take charge of the team’s first match at Cardiff on Wednesday.

West Ham sit eighth in the Championship after defeats in their last two matches. Parker, who has promoted Burnley, Bournemouth and Fulham, is expected to use his promotion experience to spark a revival.
summary: Scott Parker has been confirmed as West Ham’s head coach, taking over from Nuno Espírito Santo, who was sacked on Tuesday. The 46‑year‑old former midfielder, who has guided Burnley, Bournemouth and Fulham to the Premier League, signed a two‑and‑a‑half‑year deal and will lead the eighth‑placed Championship side in his first match at Cardiff on Wednesday.

title: James Milner beats Muzzy Izzet for fastest footballer marathon time
content: Plus: managers sacked after signing new deals, war victims commemorated on kits and the first club website (part II) Mail us with all of your questions and answers It came as no surprise to the Knowledge that James Milner had spent the early months of his retirement training for – and then running in – the New York City Marathon. Yes, the bleep test-loving former Brighton, Liverpool and Manchester City player recorded an excellent time of 3hr 9min 4sec, an average of 7min 13sec per mile. Not bad for a 40-year-old whose physique is more like that of a wrestler than a whippet. “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00,” he said, lamenting his late-career injuries for hindering him. In 2012 we ran a column listing footballers’ fastest marathon times, with the former Leicester playmaker Muzzy Izzet leading the pack on 3hr 22min 36sec at the 2011 London Marathon. That very respectable time has now been surpassed by the Premier League’s record appearance maker, so we thought we had better take a gulp of our isotonic energy drink and run through a few more tales of football’s marathon men and women.
summary: James Milner recorded a time of 3 hours 9 minutes 4 seconds at the New York City Marathon, surpassing Muzzy Izzet's previous record of 3 hours 22 minutes 36 seconds. This achievement makes the former Brighton, Liverpool, and Manchester City player the fastest marathoner among footballers.

content:
Qatar has withdrawn from hosting the 2028 Nations Championship finals due to uncertainty stemming from the war in the Middle East. This decision also resulted in the cancellation of a planned title sponsorship deal with Qatar Airways. Following months of negotiations, both parties agreed to terminate an agreement that would have seen Qatar stage the six-match final series in 2028 and 2032, alongside a title sponsorship for four editions of the competition.

Paris’s Stade de France is now the most likely venue for the 2028 finals. The cancellation of the sponsorship arrangement with the national airline was part of the broader agreement to withdraw from the hosting and sponsorship commitments.

content:

The article’s provided text also includes a narrative segment set in Tombstone, Arizona, just south of Tucson. It describes Boothill Graveyard on the town’s outskirts as the final resting place for cowboys who died “with their boots on” during deadly wild west shootouts.

title: Flint scientist Dr Siddhartha Roy wins 2026 Maddox Prize
content:
Dr. Siddhartha Roy, a third-year PhD student during the Flint, Michigan, water crisis, was part of a scientific team that publicly contradicted state and federal assertions that the lead-contaminated water was safe. This stance initially established him as a local hero. However, his reputation shifted after new research challenged the notion that children in Flint had suffered permanent brain damage from the crisis.

Roy’s commitment to adhering to the evidence, regardless of the resulting offense, has led to him receiving the 2026 Maddox prize. This award recognizes individuals who champion science and evidence in the face of challenges or hostility. In an interview with Ian Sample, Roy discusses his reflections on the Flint experience and notes that his work in the area caused him to lose friends.
summary: Dr Siddhartha Roy, a former PhD student, won the 2026 Maddox Prize for standing up for science during the Flint water crisis. He initially became a local hero for contradicting claims that the water was safe, but later faced criticism when new research challenged findings on permanent brain damage in children.

title: UN report finds rich nations' climate adaptation funding lags behind needs
content:
A United Nations report has found that financial support pledged by wealthy nations for climate‑adaptation measures in poorer countries has stalled. According to the report, flows of money to help vulnerable states cope with the climate crisis have been flat or even falling since 2022, even as extreme weather events increase and scientists warn that global warming may be accelerating.

The report details that adaptation funding—intended for stronger infrastructure, early warning systems, flood protection and drought‑resilient irrigation—remains woefully short of what is required. It also notes that the assistance is far below the promises made by rich countries in 2021, which themselves were already considered inadequate given those nations’ greater responsibility for the crisis.
summary: The UN report says financial support promised by rich nations for climate adaptation is far below what is needed. Flows of money to help poor countries have been flat or falling since 2022, even as extreme weather impacts grow and scientists warn global heating may be accelerating.

content:

The Center for Wild Animal Welfare (CWAW) argues this reduction is necessary to ease acute stress on birds and other animals. They contend that a 90dB limit, which is approximately one-eighth as loud as 120dB, would significantly reduce the area disturbed by fireworks, thereby safeguarding millions of wild animals.

The organization is pushing ministers to go beyond the previously proposed cut to 110 decibels. CWAW states that the more drastic reduction to 90 decibels would better address the acute stress caused to wildlife, ensuring a more substantial protection for animals affected by firework displays.
summary: UK campaigners push for firework noise limit cut to 90dB to protect wildlife.

content:

This ability to recall sequences of events and associations helps guide actions in new scenarios.
summary: Neurons in the hippocampus separate different aspects of experiences. When remembering an experience, people recall where it happened, its timing, and how it unfolded over time, which helps them recall sequences of events and associations that guide their actions in new scenarios.

title: Wild Animals Self-Deploy GPS Collars Using New Capture-Free Telemetry
content:

A new approach developed at the Norwegian University of Life Sciences (NMBU) allows GPS collars to be deployed autonomously on free-roaming terrestrial wildlife. This technique, known as Capture-Free Telemetry (CFT), places tracking devices on wild animals as they interact with baited deployment units in their natural habitat.

The proof-of-concept study, published in BioScience, demonstrates the feasibility of this self-collaring method. By eliminating the need for physical capture, the approach offers a new way to study wild animals using GPS technology.
summary: Researchers have long struggled to attach GPS collars to wild animals because they must be captured. title: One Third of Infants with Peanut Allergy Outgrow It Within First Year
content:
A recent study published in The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology: In Practice reports that more than a third of infants previously diagnosed with peanut allergy no longer react to peanuts during subsequent testing. The research, conducted by the Murdoch Children’s Research Institute in Melbourne, involved 778 babies who had been diagnosed with peanut allergy and then underwent an oral food challenge. In the challenge, infants were given gradually increasing doses of peanut flour up to 2,500 milligrams—equivalent to two teaspoons of peanut butter—under medical supervision. The study found that 35 percent of the babies did not react to any dose, despite having shown rashes, swelling, hives, or other allergic symptoms after consuming peanut-containing foods and having skin prick or blood test results consistent with a peanut allergy.

The oral food challenge was carried out before the national oral immunotherapy programme, which has been offered free to all Australian babies diagnosed with peanut allergy under 12 months of age since 2024. The programme, overseen by ten public children’s hospitals, involves feeding small but gradually increasing doses of peanut flour over two years to desensitise infants. Parents of the 35 percent who passed the challenge were informed that their child was no longer considered to have a peanut allergy, could safely reintroduce peanut at home, and did not need to begin the immunotherapy programme.

The average time between initial diagnosis and the oral food challenge was six months, leaving unclear why a third of infants stopped reacting to peanut in such a short period. Dr. Tim Brettig, the medical lead of the programme, suggested that the infants may have had a transient allergy, where the immune system initially reacts aberrantly to a food but the response does not persist. Previous research has shown that roughly a third of children with peanut allergies naturally grow out of them by age six, but this is the first time a high proportion of peanut allergies have been found to resolve on their own in infants.

The findings have implications for how peanut allergy is diagnosed and managed. Dr. John Ziegler of the University of New South Wales noted that peanut allergy is often diagnosed based on clinical history and skin prick or blood tests without an oral food challenge. Routinely conducting oral food challenges could identify infants who do not need treatment and be cost‑effective. He emphasized that the study confirms the importance of confirming the diagnosis of peanut allergy before starting oral immunotherapy. The researchers caution that allergy treatments should only be conducted under medical supervision due to the risk of severe reactions such as anaphylaxis.
summary: In a study of 778 Australian infants previously diagnosed with peanut allergy, 35 per cent passed an oral food challenge and were found not to react to peanut flour. The findings suggest that a surprisingly high proportion of infants’ peanut allergies resolve within the first year, potentially eliminating the need for lifelong avoidance and treatment.

title: Stanford researchers discover molecule that suppresses appetite and promotes weight loss
content:
Stanford researchers discovered an AI‑identified natural molecule that suppresses appetite and promotes fat loss in animals, offering a potential Ozempic‑like weight‑loss treatment without the common digestive side effects or significant muscle loss.

The molecule, called BRP, reduced food intake by up to 50% and targets a different brain pathway, raising hopes for a more precise obesity treatment if future human trials prove successful.
summary: Stanford researchers discover molecule that suppresses appetite and promotes weight loss.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists discover compound that enhances muscle‑repair protein to 'Super HGF'
content: Scientists have discovered a compound that transforms a natural muscle‑repair protein into a more powerful version dubbed “Super HGF,” more than doubling its ability to bind to a key receptor while protecting it from age‑related chemical damage. Early mouse experiments support the breakthrough, which could eventually help combat muscle loss and preserve strength as people age.
summary: Scientists discovered a compound that turns a natural muscle‑repair protein into a more powerful version called 'Super HGF'. Early mouse experiments show the compound more than doubles the protein's ability to bind to a key receptor and protects it from age‑related chemical damage, potentially helping combat muscle loss as people age.
author: Science Daily

title: MIT scientists break a 20-year rule and unlock never-before-seen crystal structures
content: MIT scientists have overturned a two‑decade rule by showing that flexible molecular connections, rather than rigid ones, can unlock entirely new arrangements of nanoparticles. This discovery challenges conventional thinking about nanoparticle assembly. The breakthrough could enable a new generation of designer materials with unusual properties, potentially impacting electronics, medicine, and energy applications.
summary: MIT scientists have challenged two decades of conventional thinking by discovering that flexible molecular connections, rather than rigid ones, can unlock entirely new ways to arrange nanoparticles. The breakthrough could lead to a new generation of designer materials with unusual properties and applications in electronics, medicine, and energy.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA looks for private companies to boost Hubble into higher orbit
content:
NASA is exploring a plan to prevent the Hubble Space Telescope from falling into Earth's atmosphere. After more than 35 years of operation, the telescope is losing altitude and could reenter the atmosphere as early as 2033 or 2034 without intervention.

To extend Hubble's operational life, NASA is soliciting proposals from private space companies. These firms are asked to suggest innovative methods to boost the observatory into a higher orbit, upgrade its capabilities, or safely dispose of it when its mission concludes.
summary: NASA is exploring a plan to keep the Hubble Space Telescope from falling back to Earth as early as 2033 or 2034. The agency is asking private space companies to propose ways to boost Hubble into a higher orbit, upgrade its capabilities, or safely dispose of it when its mission ends.
author: Science Daily

title: SLAC scientists confirm third type of magnetism, altermagnetism
content:
SLAC scientists have confirmed the existence of a third type of magnetism, known as altermagnetism, challenging the nearly 90-year belief that magnetism consists of only two categories. By utilizing specialized X-rays, the researchers identified a unique magnetic signature that distinguishes these materials from conventional magnets.

Altermagnets offer a combination of stability and efficient information carrying, which could address significant limitations in current electronics. This discovery holds potential for developing faster computers, more efficient data centers, and advancements in quantum technology.
summary: Researchers at SLAC used specialized X-rays to discover a unique magnetic signature that confirms the existence of a third type of magnetism, altermagnetism. Altermagnets are stable and can efficiently carry information, offering potential improvements for electronics, data centers, and quantum technology.
author: Science Daily

title: Very good boys? The dark, dystopian rise of robot dogs | Arwa Mahwadi
content:
Arwa Mahwadi’s article explores the expanding role of robot dogs in the United States, contrasting their potential utility with concerns over their military and law enforcement applications. The piece highlights the purchase of mechanical canines by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the development of "mutant mutts" by a startup named Warhound. These developments prompt questions about the nature of these machines, which lack fur and faces but contain technology such as shoulder chips.

In San Francisco, a startup called Dimensional is paying individuals $20 (£15) an hour to walk four-legged robot dogs. This initiative is not for exercise but to generate training data for the company. As reported by the New York Times, the objective is to create operating systems that integrate with AI agents, enabling the machines to act more independently.

While the specific future actions of these autonomous robots remain undefined, Dimensional’s founder asserts that the technology will assist people. One cited example is the potential for the robots to carry groceries, a task the author notes their small chihuahua-mix cannot perform.
summary: Pups that carry your shopping are one thing – but what about the mechanical canines being bought up in the US by ICE? Or the mutant mutts due to be developed by a startup called Warhound?
author: Guardian Science

title: NZ astrophotographer Brendan Larsen fights AI creation claims over satellite image
content:
Brendan Larsen spent two hours in September photographing the night sky over Mount Taranaki on New Zealand’s North Island, capturing hundreds of exposures that combine into a single image showing thousands of satellites crossing the sky. The photograph has been viewed millions of times online.

The striking picture has led some observers to claim it was generated by artificial intelligence. Larsen, the astrophotographer behind the work, is contesting those accusations, maintaining that the image was produced entirely from his own photographs.
summary: Brendan Larsen spent two hours in September taking hundreds of photographs of the night sky over Mount Taranaki, producing an image that shows thousands of satellites cross‑hatching the sky. The image, which has been viewed millions of times online, has led to accusations that it was created by AI, which Larsen is fighting.
author: Guardian Science

title: Gemini Trains on Personal Chat History Even for Paid Subscribers
content: If you have a personal Google AI subscription, all your saved chat history in Gemini can be used for training and there is no way to opt out unless you turn off chat history or use temporary chat sessions. These chat transcripts may even be read by human reviewers. Although Google claims to disconnect them from your account when human-reviewed, they explicitly warn not to enter confidential information. Https://support. Google. Com/gemini/answer/16836988 “[Gemini app activity] is used to improve Google services for everyone, including by training generative AI models, if your Keep Activity setting is on.“ https://support. Google. Com/gemini/answer/13594961? Hl=en#human_review “A subset of chats are reviewed by human reviewers” https://support. Google. Com/gemini/answer/13594961? Hl=en#pn_retain_data “Chats reviewed by human reviewers [...] are not deleted when you delete your activity. Instead, they are retained for up to three years.” https://support. Google. Com/gemini/answer/13594961? Hl=en#pn_data_usage “Please don’t enter confidential information that you wouldn’t want a reviewer to see or Google to use to improve our services, including machine-learning technologies.” To disable their training on your chat sessions, you need to turn off “Keep Activity” in Gemini’s settings. Turning that off means you’ll lose any chat sessions after 72 hours. I learned this too late, thinking that having a paid subscription = not being turned into the product. Apparently paying is not enough. Thank you to this user on HN for mentioning in another thread: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50355424 Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50363461 Points: 308 # Comments: 84
summary: If you have a personal Google AI subscription, all your saved chat history in Gemini can be used for training and there is no way to opt out unless you turn off chat history or use temporary chat sessions. These chat transcripts may even be read by human reviewers.
author: Hacker News

title: Enterprise AI security requires data lineage to trace agentic data flows
content:
A recent report highlights a data‑lineage issue that surfaced when a sales representative requested pricing from an AI agent. The agent accessed restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes, producing a proposal that appeared correct to the agent. A second agent then drafted the proposal for the sales rep, but no human reviewed either handoff. The final document contained unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information. Because the workflow involved multiple agents and systems, the source of the problematic data could not be traced, nor could its spread across files and agents be understood.

The report argues that this scenario demonstrates the need for AI governance to evolve quickly. As enterprises adopt agentic AI in everyday operations, they must manage not only static files but also moving, fragmented data that is continuously ingested, copied, summarized, transformed, reused, and redistributed. It concludes that AI security is a data visibility problem, not merely a tool issue. Traditional security models focused on applications, systems, networks, or endpoints are insufficient. To secure agentic AI at scale, organizations must establish data lineage to manage governance, accountability, and trust across human, agentic, and hybrid workflows.
summary: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Joyn blended meat debut, PRIMA implant restores vision, AI agents enable agentic web
content: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. These startups hope “blended” food will cut our appetite for red meat In the fall of 2025, Jeff Dodge served hungry students steaming marinara sauce and meatballs. The students loved them: 92% of those who tried them wanted them on the menu. Few could guess that mushrooms had been mixed into the meat. Dodge was testing a new product called 50/Cut from the company Joyn. The blend of seemingly simple ingredients—available as meatballs, burgers, and ground meat—could help solve one of the biggest challenges of the climate crisis: getting people to eat less meat, particularly beef. Joyn is among a wave of startups creating “blended meat,” which combines plant proteins with the real deal. The logic: The best meat replacement is … better meat. Get a taste of the startups betting on greener beef. —Meghan McCarron This implant can restore sight for patients with macular degeneration More than 5 million people have an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) called geographic atrophy, in which retinal cells die off. Until now, no treatment could restore their vision. A system called PRIMA changes that. It combines a retinal implant with camera-equipped eyeglasses to improve sight in patients who develop a blind spot in the middle of their vision. After training sessions, more than 80% of recipients could read, do crosswords, and use their phones. Find out how the sight-restoring implant works. —Linda Marsa MIT Technology Review Narrated: The agentic web is here In 2001, a decade after inventing the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision: an internet navigated by autonomous software agents that address our every need, without requiring us to muck about with browsers and search engines ourselves. At the time, the idea seemed far-fetched. But a quarter-century on, AI agents are beginning to make it a reality. They can triage your inbox, do your grocery shopping, and even access your bank accounts. This new era is being called the agentic web, and it will inevitably transform the internet. Whether the human web survives this transition is anyone’s guess. This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts. Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released.
