title: Study finds natural selection in Chernobyl dogs, cause unknown
content: A new study reports evidence of natural selection occurring in the dogs living around Chernobyl. While genetic differences have been identified, researchers have not determined the factors driving these changes or the potential evolutionary benefits they might confer.
summary: A new study found evidence of natural selection in the dogs of Chernobyl. Scientists said it is still unclear what drove the genetic differences or what evolutionary advantages they may provide.
author: Wired

title: New Jersey ebike law mandates licenses, sometimes insurance, causing rider confusion
content: New Jersey’s new electric‑bike law, effective early 2026, requires owners to obtain a license and, in some cases, insurance before riding. The requirement has left many riders stranded and confused about the new obligations.
summary: Since early 2026, New Jersey’s law has required electric bike owners to obtain licenses and, in some cases, insurance to ride. The requirement has left many riders stranded and confused.
author: Wired

title: Differences Between Ebikes and E‑Motos Explained for Buyers
content: The piece notes that riders and lawmakers often confuse e‑bikes with e‑motos, and that some retailers may deliberately blur the distinction. It then offers guidance to help consumers select the micromobility vehicle that truly meets their needs.
summary: Riders and lawmakers often don’t know the difference between an ebike and an e‑moto. Retailers sometimes muddy the waters, and the guide shows how to buy the micromobility vehicle you actually want.
author: Wired

title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remains timeless
content:
Breath of the Wild, released two decades after the series’ shift to three‑dimensional gameplay, “changed everything” for The Legend of Zelda franchise, according to the source. The game emphasized an open‑ended adventure that let players move freely and approach challenges in multiple ways, moving away from a fixed path.

The article notes that this design philosophy has carried over to later titles such as Tears of the Kingdom and Echoes of Wisdom, expanding the series’ scale and reducing the prominence of traditional, more linear Zelda games.
summary: According to the article, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time never gets old. Breath of the Wild transformed the franchise with an open‑ended adventure focused on player freedom, a philosophy that continues in later games such as Tears of the Kingdom and Echoes of Wisdom.
author: The Verge

title: Alphabet reports search revenue growth slows to 12% as paid click growth drops to 8%
content:
Alphabet’s latest earnings report showed that search queries are increasing at the fastest pace in five years. Despite this uptick, the company’s search‑related revenue grew 12 percent year over year in the third quarter, a slowdown from the roughly 17 percent increase recorded in the prior quarter.  

Paid‑click growth, which reflects clicks on ads that generate revenue for Google, also decelerated, falling from a 13 percent rise to an 8 percent rise. The company plans to spend about $200 billion this year on infrastructure, much of it aimed at supporting artificial‑intelligence initiatives.  

Since the earnings release, Alphabet’s shares have declined about 14 percent. The data illustrate that while overall search activity is expanding, the pace of revenue and ad‑click growth has moderated.
summary: Google Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler. | Bloomberg via Getty Images Search queries are growing at their fastest rate in five years, Google parent Alphabet said in its earnings report last week.
author: The Verge

title: Study finds TV opt‑out blocks data on most brands but Samsung, Roku, Vizio still track
content:
Researchers at Northeastern University examined whether opting out of automatic content recognition (ACR) on modern televisions actually prevents data collection. The team monitored twelve TVs representing ten manufacturers and evaluated the impact of the opt‑out setting on each device.

The study found that opting out stopped most of the data transmission for several brands, including LG, Amazon Fire TV, a Sony Bravia running Google TV, and televisions that use the Vidaa OS platform—found on models from Hisense, Toshiba and smaller manufacturers such as Supersonic. In contrast, Samsung and Roku devices continued to send some viewing information even after users selected the opt‑out option.

Additionally, a Vizio television sold through Walmart persisted in transmitting data as though the opt‑out had never been applied. The findings highlight that while many TV makers honor the opt‑out request, certain brands still retain the ability to collect viewing data despite user preferences.
summary: Researchers at Northeastern University monitored 12 TVs from 10 manufacturers to test if opting out of automatic content recognition stops data collection. Opting out prevented data transmission on most devices—including LG, Amazon Fire TV, Sony Bravia with Google TV, and Vidaa OS TVs—but Samsung, Roku, and Walmart’s Vizio TV continued to send some information.
author: The Verge

title: SpaceX teams with Qualcomm to use Dragonwing tech at 5G sites by 2027
content:
SpaceX has entered a multi‑year partnership with Qualcomm to incorporate the chipmaker’s Dragonwing technology into its planned Starlink Mobile 5G network. The agreement calls for Dragonwing to be deployed at “tens of thousands” of 5G cell sites across the United States, with the first installations slated for 2027.  

The collaboration is presented as part of SpaceX’s effort to position Starlink Mobile as a major U.S. carrier, directly competing with T‑Mobile, AT&T and Verizon. The company has already acquired a substantial amount of spectrum and recent reports noted it was looking at a possible acquisition of Boost Mobile.
summary: SpaceX is teaming up with Qualcomm to build out its nationwide mobile network. Under the multi-year deal, SpaceX will bring Qualcomm's Dragonwing technology to "tens of thousands" of 5G cell sites across the US, with the first deployments set for 2027.
author: The Verge

title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman defends RAM stance, changes X name to “Ram Altman”
content: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman spent election night defending his position on PC RAM purchases. He changed his name on X to "Ram Altman" in response to another user's comment, saying, "i actually do want the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers, and it is fucking annoying that this was taken out of context. I have been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time." He replied to another comment, saying, "i want you to have so much ram lets build more." but only because…i actually do want the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers …
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman spent election night defending his position on PC RAM purchases. He changed his name on X to “Ram Altman” and said he wants the world to have tons of memory and for people to put as much as they want in their computers.
author: The Verge

title: Nintendo Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time hailed as modern masterpiece
content: Nintendo Switch 2; Nintendo This ambitious remake transforms a landmark Zelda game into a modern masterpiece, clearer and easier to navigate, more beautiful to look at, with playful musical touches. Yet the melancholy remains It’s always a worry, returning to a formative piece of art from your childhood. Will your jaded adult sensibilities render you unable to locate the magic that captivated your child self? Will revisiting it reveal that it was never actually that good, and that your tastes are built on a foundation of lies? With video games, there is the added complication of technological advancement: decades-old games can look so basic and feel so treacly to play that it’s hard to explain why they were mind-blowing at the time. Light-touch remasters aim to bring such games up to modern graphical standards without fundamentally changing them; an ambitious remake attempts to transform the work into something that can stand alongside any modern masterpiece. Ocarina of Time is the latter. And I could not be more delighted to report that it is a dream come true.
summary: The ambitious Nintendo Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time transforms the landmark game into a clearer, easier‑to‑navigate and more beautiful modern masterpiece with playful musical touches. The reviewer calls the result a dream come true despite the lingering melancholy.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Titanium Court blends 8-bit strategy, match‑3 and surprise musical boss fights
content: Titanium Court is a bizarre world of 8-bit fairies, Shakespeare and surprise songs – its magic lies in never knowing what on earth is going on • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here Earlier this year, I was stuck in hospital for several days, fuzzy on pain medication and bored out of my mind, with nothing but a Steam Deck for company. In the middle of one of those long nights, unable to sleep, I played a game called Titanium Court. It’s a strange creation that looks like it was made for the ZX Spectrum and reads like a postmodern Shakespeare adaptation – a compelling mix of strategy game and match-3 where you rearrange battlefields by matching tiles, before sending tiny lo-fi fairy armies to their deaths. At the end of this late-night run, I met a boss I’d defeated before – a comically hungry dragon – and the game asked if I would like to skip the boss fight and enjoy a musical performance instead. A game has never asked me this before. Of course, I accepted. And then, instead of the familiar tiled battlefield, I was looking at a pixellated singer-songwriter, who launched into an extremely long preamble about the mating habits of the Pacific salmon before saying, “This is a song for anyone else who ever got so horny they could die,” and launching into a soulful acoustic guitar number accompanied by crude images of leaping fish. I began to wonder if my meds were making me hallucinate.
summary: Titanium Court is an 8‑bit‑style game that mixes strategy, match‑3 gameplay and post‑modern Shakespeare elements. When a dragon boss is defeated, the game can offer to skip the fight and play a musical performance by a pixellated singer‑songwriter about Pacific salmon.
author: Guardian Technology

title: UK Home Office to use facial recognition in biggest immigration crackdown
content: Documents show Home Office developing programme to use technology for general immigration enforcement The Home Office is preparing to deploy facial recognition technology at transport hubs and public events as part of the biggest immigration enforcement crackdown in British history. Policy documents show the government has been developing a programme to deploy live facial recognition (LFR) cameras for “general immigration enforcement”, including non-criminal immigration offences.
summary: The Home Office is preparing to deploy live facial recognition cameras at transport hubs and public events. The programme is part of the biggest immigration enforcement crackdown in British history and will target general immigration offences, including non‑criminal ones.
author: Guardian Technology

title: House Speaker Mike Johnson says Republicans will retake the House in 2028
content: U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson told Republicans not to lose hope after Democrats achieved major gains in the 2026 midterm elections. Johnson said the party will double down on its agenda and work to retake the House in the 2028 election.
summary: House Speaker Mike Johnson urged Republicans not to lose hope after Democrats made major gains in the 2026 midterm elections. He pledged that Republicans will double down on their agenda and aim to retake the House in 2028.
author: Euronews

title: 33 killed and over 50 missing after Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia aid site
content: Russian strikes on a humanitarian aid site in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region on Monday, 2 November, killed 33 people and left more than 50 missing. Survivors and rescuers are receiving treatment for severe injuries.
summary: Russian strikes on a humanitarian aid site in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region killed 33 people and left more than 50 missing on Monday 2 November. Survivors and rescuers are being treated for severe injuries.
author: Euronews

title: Iranian MP Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani says Tehran will strike Europe if US uses its bases
content: Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani, a member of Iranian parliament’s security committee, said Iran would fire on any European base used against it, including in Italy and Germany. State-run media said any new confrontation could reach “the heart of Europe".
summary: Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani, a member of Iran's parliament security committee, said Iran would fire on any European base used against it, including in Italy and Germany. State-run media warned that a new confrontation could reach the heart of Europe.
author: Euronews

title: Housing protesters set up around 100 tents in Lisbon's Rossio Square after court ruling
content:
Housing protesters have returned to Lisbon’s historic Rossio Square, where they have set up around 100 tents following a court ruling.  

The demonstration comes as Portugal’s government faces growing pressure over housing.
summary: Housing protesters have returned to Lisbon's historic Rossio Square, setting up around 100 tents after a court ruling. The demonstration comes as Portugal's government faces growing pressure over housing.
author: Euronews

title: Hockey nations refuse to play Russia as Germany weighs pulling out as host
content: Finland, Norway, the Czech Republic, Latvia, Denmark and Sweden have announced they will not play Russia at the 2027 championship after a court overturned a four‑year ban on Russian national teams. Germany’s federation said the ruling “fundamentally changes the situation” for it as host nation.
summary: Finland, Norway, the Czech Republic, Latvia, Denmark and Sweden have said they will not face Russia at the 2027 championship, after a court ruling overturned a four-year ban on Russian national teams. Germany’s federation said the ruling “fundamentally changes the situation” for it as host nation.
author: Euronews

title: US expert warns post‑midterm Trump will be weaker but more aggressive toward Europe
content: After the U.S. midterm elections, Europe will not see a weakened Donald Trump but one who is expected to focus even more on global politics, warns U.S. expert Josef Braml. Braml cautions that Europe cannot afford to wait for a different Trump, as the current administration’s foreign‑policy approach could pose a greater threat.
summary: After the midterms, Europe will not get a weaker Trump but one who turns even more to global politics, warns US expert Josef Braml. Europe cannot wait this Trump out.
author: Euronews

title: Trump’s Approval Rating Falls to 37.3% Amid Midterm Democratic Victory
content: Donald Trump’s declining popularity has been cited as a major factor in the Democrats’ sweeping victory in the midterms.  Recent polls show his approval rating has dropped to 37.3%, down from 42% during his first midterm election.
summary: Trump’s unpopularity is cited as a major factor in the Democrats’ sweeping victory in the midterms. Latest polls show his approval rating plummeted to 37.3%, down from 42% in his first midterm election.
author: France 24

title: Ukrainians See No Immediate Effect from US Midterm Democratic Victory on Russia War
content: Ukrainians say they do not anticipate a rapid or substantial shift in U.S. policy toward the war with Russia following the Democrats’ victory in the midterm elections, according to France 24 correspondent Emmanuelle Chaze in Kyiv. President Volodymyr Zelensky has not yet commented on the “blue wave” now controlling Congress.
summary: Ukrainians See No Immediate Effect from US Midterm Democratic Victory on Russia War.
author: France 24

title: Democrats' midterm win gives Donald Trump a blue House budget challenge
content: The Democrats’ win in the midterm elections has put Donald Trump in a challenging spot for the remainder of his term. With a now “blue” House of Representatives, the budget will be set by Congress, and Trump will have to accept and follow it. France 24’s international affairs editor Philip Turle reports on the situation.
summary: The Democrats' victory in the midterm elections has given them control of the House of Representatives, now a "blue" chamber that will set the budget. This leaves Donald Trump in a difficult position for the rest of his mandate, according to France 24’s international affairs editor Philip Turle.
author: France 24

title: Trump shifts blame for GOP midterm loss, says he could have won
content:
Donald Trump has tried to shift blame for the Republican Party’s defeat in the midterm elections, asserting that the party would have won had he been on the ballot.  

France 24’s Washington correspondent Fraser Jackson counters that the “blue wave” that gave Democrats control of Congress can be traced directly back to Trump’s decisions.
summary: Donald Trump has sought to shift the blame for the Republicans' defeat at the midterms by claiming that if he had been on the ballot the party would have won. France 24's Washington correspondent Fraser Jackson says the blue wave that gave Democrats control of Congress can be traced directly back to Trump's decisions.
author: France 24

title: Abdul El-Sayed Set to Become First Muslim US Senator After Michigan Midterm Victory
content: Abdul El-Sayed is set to become the first Muslim senator in US history following his midterms victory in Michigan. His victory came despite what he has denounced as racist attacks against him, inlcuding from Donald Trump, which, says FRANCE 24's correspondent Jessica Le Masurier, he rebuffed with a mixture of "humour and hope".
summary: Abdul El-Sayed is set to become the first Muslim senator in US history after winning the Michigan midterms. He rebuffed racist attacks, including from Donald Trump, with humour and hope, according to Jessica Le Masurier of FRANCE 24.
author: France 24

title: Trump says inflation hurt Republicans in midterms, cites Iran war
content: Speaking to Fox News following the midterm elections, US President Donald Trump admitted that inflation was likely one reason Republicans did poorly. Many Americans have been frustrated with how the Iran war has pushed up prices, including at the gasoline pump, especially given that Trump had campaigned for his second term on a pledge of “no new wars”, as Ellen Gainsford explains.
summary: Trump says inflation hurt Republicans in midterms, cites Iran war.
author: France 24

title: Gen Z backs Democrats with 75% support in US midterm elections
content: In the U.S. midterm elections, 50 million members of Gen Z were eligible to vote. Young voters gave Democrats the strongest support, with 75 % of them voting for the party. The generation is expected to become the largest voting bloc in the United States in the coming years. FRANCE 24’s Ophelie Jacobson has more.
summary: In the US midterm elections, 50 million Gen Z members were eligible to vote. Seventy‑five percent of those young voters voted for the Democrats.
author: France 24

title: French blood banks stop cyberattack on refrigerated blood storage units
content: French authorities reported that a cyberattack in France aimed at three cold‑storage facilities holding donated blood samples and plasma. The attempt was thwarted by the facilities’ alarm systems, preventing any successful breach. This incident follows a series of suspected attacks on refrigeration units in European supermarkets and, on the same day, on the French cooperative bank Credit Mutuel Arkea. The latest effort underscores ongoing attempts to compromise refrigerated equipment across various sectors.
summary: A cyberattack in France targeted three cold stores that held donated blood samples and plasma, authorities said on Wednesday. The incident was unsuccessful because the facilities' alarm systems triggered, and it follows other suspected refrigerator attacks in European supermarkets and at the French cooperative bank Credit Mutuel Arkea.
author: France 24

title: Wawira Njiru wins German Africa Prize for Kenyan school feeding scheme
content: Wawira Njiru’s Kenyan school‑feeding scheme, which began as a small fundraiser and has grown into a major enterprise, is being recognized with the German Africa Prize. The award acknowledges the unexpected success of her initiative to provide meals for schoolchildren.
summary: Wawira Njiru's Kenyan school feeding scheme has grown from a small fundraiser into a major enterprise. She is being awarded the German Africa Prize.
author: DW World

title: Indonesia deploys troops to Jakarta over wiretapping allegations
content: Indonesian troops have been stationed in Jakarta following allegations of illegal wiretapping. The accusations involve the president’s chief of staff, with suspects said to have tapped the president’s phones. The deployment is a direct response to these allegations.
summary: Indonesian troops have been deployed to Jakarta as wiretapping allegations involving the president's chief of staff emerge. The suspects are accused of illegally tapping the president's phones.
author: DW World

title: Democrats' midterm win tied to economic concerns over oil, tariffs and debt
content:
Economic issues such as high oil prices, data‑center costs, tariffs and rising debt were cited as major factors in the decisive loss suffered by President Donald Trump’s Republican candidates in the midterm elections.  

The article then asks whether the victorious Democrats will be able to influence the U.S. economy moving forward.
summary: Economic concerns including high oil prices, data centers, tariffs and mounting debt helped cause the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. The Democrats' midterm win raises the question of whether they can make a difference.
author: DW World

title: UNEP report says climate adaptation financing far short as warming set to exceed 1.5°C
content: The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) reported on Wednesday that, despite projections that global warming will surpass the 1.5 °C threshold, the amount of financing available to help communities adapt to climate change is far below the level required. The report highlights a significant shortfall in adaptation funding as the planet continues to warm.
summary: Global warming is set to exceed 1.5°C. A UN Environment Programme report published on Wednesday said financing to help communities adapt to climate change falls far short of needs.
author: UN News

title: Afghan children face narrowing path to education, UN agencies report
content: UN agencies report that more than half of Afghanistan’s children who should be in primary school are not enrolled in formal education. The same reports note that millions of Afghan girls can only dream of attending university, highlighting a shrinking path to learning.
summary: More than half of Afghanistan’s children who should be in primary school remain outside formal learning and millions of girls can only dream of going to university.
author: UN News

title: Over 900 academics urge UK to reverse ban on climate scholar Andreas Malm
content: Blocking Swedish writer’s entry for event with Palestine Action co-founder is attack on free expression, letter says More than 900 academics have voiced their opposition to the government’s decision to block the climate academic Andreas Malm from entering the UK, warning that the move represents “a grave violation of academic freedom and freedom of expression”. Malm, the author of How to Blow Up a Pipeline and a leading climate scholar, was prevented from entering the UK last week by the Home Office after being told that his presence in the UK “may not be considered to be conducive to the public good”.
summary: More than 900 academics have opposed the UK government's decision to block climate academic Andreas Malm from entering the country. The Home Office said his presence “may not be considered to be conducive to the public good” and prevented his entry last week.
author: Guardian World

title: Hackers raise temperatures at three French blood product cold stores, EFS says
content: Temperature and defrosting thresholds raised to ‘very high levels’ at three cold stores stocking vital blood products Europe live – latest updates France’s national blood service has said hackers accessed control systems and boosted temperatures at three cold stores stocking vital blood products, in an apparent escalation of recent cyber-attacks on fridges and freezers across Europe. The French blood service (EFS) said temperature and defrosting thresholds had been raised to “very high levels” in the attack, adding that its alarm systems had allowed technicians to intervene before the products were compromised.
summary: France’s national blood service (EFS) said hackers accessed control systems and raised temperature and defrosting thresholds to “very high levels” at three cold stores stocking vital blood products. Alarm systems alerted technicians, who intervened before the products were compromised.
author: Guardian World

title: Zelenskyy says 40 confirmed dead after Russian attack on school in Zaporizhzhia
content: School in Komyshuvakha in the Zaporizhzhia region was struck on Monday Meanwhile, the Kremlin said that ⁠it ​hopes that the ⁠results of the US ⁠midterm ​elections ‌will not impact ‌what it ‌said were president Donald Trump’s “peacemaking efforts" on Ukraine, Reuters said. In comments ‌broadcast by Russian state ​media, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said: “We ⁠are sincerely ​counting on [Trump] ​continuing ​his peacemaking ​efforts.“ “Governing in the United States will be almost impossible in the coming years given the level of internal division and polarisation. As a European politician I will mainly look of course to trade policies, ⁠support to Ukraine and Nato.”
summary: Zelenskyy said 40 people are now confirmed dead after a Russian attack on a school. The school in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, was struck on Monday.
author: Guardian World

title: Muslim Votes Matter softens anti-Labor stance ahead of Victorian election in bid to defeat One Nation in at-risk seats
content:
Muslim Votes Matter, a grassroots advocacy group, says it will soften its previously anti‑Labor stance for the upcoming Victorian state election. The organisation plans to direct its supporters to vote for the Labor Party rather than Pauline Hanson’s One Nation across all lower‑house electorates in Victoria.

To support that effort, the group intends to place volunteers on the ground in two outer‑suburban seats it identifies as vulnerable: Greenvale in Melbourne’s north and Narre Warren South in the city’s south‑east. Muslim Votes Matter warns that the incumbent Labor government risks losing these electorates to One Nation and hopes its on‑the‑ground activity will help prevent that outcome.
summary: Muslim Votes Matter softens anti-Labor stance ahead of Victorian election in bid to defeat One Nation in at-risk seats.
author: Guardian World

title: Australia’s Scanlon report: AI and cost of living concerns, multicultural support strong
content:
The 2024 Scanlon report on social cohesion in Australia reveals that cost‑of‑living pressures and concerns about artificial intelligence now rank above climate change and war as the country’s primary worries for the future.  

The report also notes that Australians are feeling poorer, increasingly pessimistic and distrustful of government.  At the same time, a global economic downturn and ongoing cost‑of‑living pressures are cited as key concerns.  

Despite these anxieties, the survey finds that a vast majority of Australians continue to support immigration and multiculturalism.
summary: The annual Scanlon report on social cohesion found that a vast majority of Australians continue to support immigration and multiculturalism despite growing feelings of poverty and distrust of government. It also showed that concerns about artificial intelligence and the cost of living now outweigh worries about climate change or war.
author: Guardian World

title: Australia’s inflation woes leave it mid‑range on global misery index
content: Australia’s inflation situation is being examined alongside that of other nations, offering a comparative view of the domestic economy. The Reserve Bank of Australia has just implemented its fifth interest‑rate increase of the year, a move that follows concerns about the country’s price pressures. In the wake of this policy action, mortgage borrowers are reported to be increasingly stressed, prompting questions about whether Australia’s inflation problem is worse than that of the rest of the world.
summary: Australia faces a severe inflation problem and the Reserve Bank delivered its fifth interest rate hike for the year. Despite this, the country ranks only around the middle of the misery index compared with other nations.
author: Guardian World

title: Albanese government warned it is ‘sleepwalking’ toward another robodebt over AI use
content:
The Centre for Public Integrity released its “Computer Says No” report on Thursday, warning that the Albanese government is “sleepwalking its way into another robodebt” scandal because of a lack of transparency and legislation surrounding the use of algorithms and artificial intelligence in governmental decisions. The report, launched by the centre’s chief executive Dr Catherine Williams, examines the government’s reliance on automated decision‑making (ADM) tools.

The think‑tank’s findings call for urgent reform, including a mandatory audit and a public register of all ADM systems used by the federal government. Williams said these measures are needed to prevent another controversy similar to the previous robodebt case.
summary: Dr Catherine Williams, chief executive of the Centre for Public Integrity, launched the “Computer Says No” report on Thursday, which examines the government’s use of automated decision‑making tools. The report warns the Albanese government is “sleepwalking its way into another robodebt” scandal and calls for a mandatory audit and public register of all such tools.
author: Guardian World

title: Endangered giant burrowing frog bred after tadpoles rescued from East Gippsland fires
content:
Following the 2019‑20 black summer bushfires, scientists in eastern Victoria discovered puddles of tadpoles belonging to the southern giant burrowing frog in East Gippsland. The frogs are one of the state’s most cryptic amphibians and are listed as critically endangered in Victoria.

The tadpoles were transported to a Melbourne zoo, where they were raised to metamorphosis and successfully bred in captivity for the first time. The bushfires had destroyed extensive areas in East Gippsland, raising concerns about the survival of the species.
summary: Scientists collected tadpoles from puddles in East Gippsland after the 2019‑20 black summer bushfires and moved them to Melbourne Zoo. The tadpoles were raised to metamorphosis and the species was bred in captivity for the first time, offering hope for the critically endangered southern giant burrowing frog.
author: Guardian World

title: Manchester City win over London City Lionesses; Ballon d’Or arrives in Bromley
content: The Women’s Football Weekly podcast features Faye Carruthers alongside Suzanne Wrack, Tom Garry and Freddie Cardy. The panel reviews the weekend’s Women’s Super League action. They highlight Manchester City’s win, noting Bunny Shaw and Lauren Hemp as key performers in the club’s victory over London City Lionesses. The discussion also covers Arsenal’s recent draw with Aston Villa and questions the most effective position for striker Alessia Russo.
summary: On the Women’s Football Weekly podcast, Bunny Shaw and Lauren Hemp led Manchester City to a win over London City Lionesses. The show also noted Arsenal’s draw with Aston Villa, debated Alessia Russo’s ideal position, and announced the Ballon d’Or will be presented in Bromley.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Arsenal win at Anfield for first time in 14 years to top Premier League
content: Arsenal secured their first league victory at Anfield in 14 years to take the top spot in the Premier League. This result was discussed on Football Weekly, where Max Rushden was joined by Barry Glendenning, Jonathan Wilson, and John Brewin. The episode also covered Manchester United’s latest defeat.
summary: Arsenal secured a league victory at Anfield for the first time in 14 years. This win moved the club to the top of the Premier League table.
author: Guardian Sport

title: AFL to consider rule changes for women's competition to suit Irish players
content:
The Australian Football League plans to review rule changes for its women’s competition to facilitate the unique style of Irish players. This initiative acknowledges the presence of nearly 50 former Gaelic footballers currently participating in the AFLW. The league’s boss indicated that the review will occur following the 2026 finals, aiming to make it easier for these athletes to incorporate their distinctive flair into the game.

A significant distinction between Australian rules and Gaelic football is the mandatory bounce required for Australian rules players running more than 15 metres. The proposed changes address this specific regulation, which differs from the rules in the sister sport. This move highlights the AFL’s intent to adapt its framework to better accommodate players transitioning from Gaelic football backgrounds.
summary: The AFL will examine rule changes in its women's competition to help Irish players incorporate their own style. This decision follows praise for Irishwoman Kearns performing an illegal double Gaelic solo.
author: Guardian Sport

title: O'Neill says Kenny's Irish family ties not important to call-up
content: Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill stated that new call-up Eoin Kenny’s family connection to the Republic of Ireland was not a factor in his selection. O'Neill selected Kenny for the senior squad ahead of this month’s Nations League matches against Ukraine and Hungary.
summary: Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill states that new call-up Eoin Kenny's family connection to the Republic of Ireland was not considered during the selection process. Kenny has been brought into the senior squad for this month's Nations League fixtures against Ukraine and Hungary.
author: BBC Sport

title: World Rugby outlines plan for safer, more continuous sport
content: World Rugby has outlined a vision for a safer and more continuous sport. This approach includes a specific desire to "embrace the contest" during the breakdown and set-piece phases of play.
summary: World Rugby has presented a vision for a safer and more continuous sport. The plan aims to embrace the contest around the breakdown and set-piece.
author: BBC Sport

title: Trailer for Rivals: Fury v Joshua Explores Boxing Rivalry
content: A new trailer for Rivals: Fury v Joshua explores the contrasting styles, personalities, and careers of Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. The content highlights how these differences shaped a rivalry that has captivated boxing fans for over a decade.
summary: A new trailer for Rivals: Fury v Joshua details how the contrasting styles, personalities, and careers of Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua shaped their rivalry. The documentary highlights a rivalry that has captivated boxing fans for more than a decade.
author: BBC Sport

title: Rahm explains reluctance to join LIV Golf 2.0 after leaving series
content: Jon Rahm explains his reluctance to join LIV Golf 2.0, saying he "wasn't willing to follow that path" after agreeing to leave the series last month.
summary: Jon Rahm stated he was not willing to follow the path of joining LIV Golf 2.0. This decision comes after he agreed to leave the series last month.
author: BBC Sport

title: Chris Gober Projected to Succeed Michael McCaul in Texas 10th District
content: Chris Gober (R) is projected to defeat Caitlin Rourk (D) in Texas’s 10th District, according to Decision Desk HQ. Gober will succeed Rep. Michael McCaul (R-Texas), who is departing Congress after more than two decades on Capitol Hill. McCaul, a 64-year-old former chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, is stepping down from his position.
summary: Chris Gober is projected to defeat Caitlin Rourk in Texas's 10th District to succeed Rep. Michael McCaul. McCaul is departing Congress after more than two decades on Capitol Hill.
author: The Hill

title: Randy Villegas Defeats Rep. David Valadeo in California 22nd District Race
content: Progressive challenger Randy Villegas (D) has defeated Rep. David Valadeo (R-Calif.) in the race for California’s 22nd Congressional District, according to a projection by Decision Desk HQ. Valadeo, who has served in the House on and off since 2013, represented both the 22nd and 21st Districts. Villegas’s victory marks the ousting of the incumbent in this battleground contest.
summary: Progressive challenger Randy Villegas (D) has defeated Rep. David Valadeo (R-Calif.) in the race for California’s 22nd Congressional District, Decision Desk HQ has projected.
author: The Hill

title: Ricketts wins reelection over independent Osborn in Nebraska Senate race
content: Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-Neb.) is projected by Decision Desk HQ to win reelection over independent challenger Dan Osborn, retaining the Nebraska Senate seat for the GOP. Ricketts, who won the 2024 special election to complete the term of former Sen. Ben Sasse (R-Neb.), is favored to secure a full six-year term in the upper chamber.
summary: Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-Neb.) fended off a Senate challenge from independent Dan Osborn, Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) projects, keeping the Nebraska seat under GOP control.
author: The Hill

title: Ex-Navy Admiral Nancy Lacore projected to win Mace's S.C. seat
content: Democrat Nancy Lacore, a former Navy Admiral dismissed by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, is projected to win South Carolina’s traditionally red House district against Republican Jenny Costa Honeycutt, according to Decision Desk HQ. The Cook Political Report recently shifted its rating for the race in Representative Nancy Mace’s (R) 1st District.
summary: Former Navy Admiral Nancy Lacore is projected to win the South Carolina 1st District House race against Republican Jenny Costa Honeycutt. The Cook Political Report shifted the traditionally red race for Rep. Nancy Mace.
author: The Hill

title: Katy Padilla Stout wins Texas 23rd District seat vacated by Tony Gonzales
content: Texas Democratic Senate candidate Katy Padilla Stout is projected to win the open 23rd Congressional District seat, which was vacated by former Rep. Tony Gonzales (R-Texas), according to preliminary results from Decision Desk HQ. Padilla Stout defeated Republican candidate Brandon Herrera, a YouTube personality and firearms advocate who held President Trump’s endorsement.
summary: Katy Padilla Stout is projected to win the open 23rd Congressional District seat in Texas. She defeated Republican candidate Brandon Herrera, who held President Trump's endorsement.
author: The Hill

title: Kristina Knickerbocker defeats Mike Turner to win Ohio 10th District seat
content: Democrat Kristina Knickerbocker is projected to win Ohio’s 10th District, defeating longtime Republican Rep. Mike Turner. According to Decision Desk HQ, Knickerbocker secured just over 49 percent of the vote, while Turner received nearly 48 percent. This result flips the seat, which the incumbent had held for more than two decades, to the Democrats.
summary: Democrat Kristina Knickerbocker is projected to win Ohio’s 10th District. She defeated longtime Rep. Mike Turner, who had held the seat for more than two decades.
author: The Hill

title: Louisiana 5th District House race heads to runoff between Moore and Firment
content: Democratic state Rep. Patricia Moore and Republican state Rep. Gabe Firment are projected to advance to a runoff for Louisiana’s 5th House District, according to Decision Desk HQ. As of 12:53 a.m. Wednesday with 93 percent of votes counted, Moore held a lead of less than one percentage point over Firment.
summary: Democratic Louisiana state Rep. Patricia Moore and Republican state Rep.
author: The Hill

title: David Crowley elected Wisconsin's first Black governor
content: Democrat David Crowley will be Wisconsin's first Black governor. He defeated Republican Congressman Tom Tiffany in a campaign that focused on lowering costs for working families and bringing more jobs to Wisconsin.
summary: Democrat David Crowley defeated Republican Congressman Tom Tiffany in the election. The campaign focused on lowering costs for working families and bringing more jobs to Wisconsin.
author: NPR Politics

title: Mamdani says midterms show working‑class power as democratic socialists celebrate historic night
content: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani told NPR's Juana Summers that the recent midterms demonstrate the power of working-class voters. He emphasized that this historic night for democratic socialists presents an opportunity for newly elected officials to seize the moment. Mamdani urged these officials to show voters what politics can deliver.
summary: Mamdani said the midterm results demonstrate the power of working‑class voters on a historic night for democratic socialists. The New York mayor told NPR’s Juana Summers that newly elected democratic socialists should seize the moment and show voters what politics can deliver.
author: NPR Politics

title: SSRS poll details how key demographic groups voted in midterms
content: Charts illustrating how key demographic groups voted in the midterm election are based on data from a poll of tens of thousands of voters. The survey was conducted by the firm SSRS for multiple news outlets, with images credited to Tommy Martino.
summary: Charts display voting patterns for various demographic groups in the recent midterm election. The data is derived from a poll of tens of thousands of voters conducted by SSRS for multiple news outlets.
author: NPR Politics

title: Troy Jackson defeats Susan Collins in Maine Senate race, a major Democratic win
content: Troy Jackson defeated Susan Collins in the Maine Senate race, marking a significant win for Democrats. This victory flips a seat that Collins had held for nearly 30 years, representing a crucial step in the Democratic effort to retake the Senate majority.
summary: Troy Jackson defeated Susan Collins in the Maine Senate race. The win flips a seat Collins has held for nearly 30 years, giving Democrats a key victory in their effort to regain the Senate majority.
author: NPR Politics

title: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries Announces America Is Back
content: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries declared “America is back” after House control was called for Democrats. He addressed supporters, arguing that voters have sent Congress a clear message to end extremism and “corruption.”
summary: Jeffries addressed supporters after House control was called for Democrats. He argued voters have sent Congress a message to end extremism and corruption.
author: NPR Politics

title: Gurez potato pits vanish, risking loss of local varieties and skills
content:
In Chorwan, a remote mountain village in Gurez, Indian-administered Kashmir, farmer Hajra Begum sorts her potato harvest for underground storage. This traditional practice allows local families to sustain themselves through the harsh Himalayan winter, with some potatoes reserved for consumption and others selected for spring planting. Begum emphasizes the importance of selecting only perfect potatoes for seed, noting that storing damaged produce can ruin the following year’s crop.

As this centuries-old storage method fades among local farmers, the article highlights a broader loss of cultural heritage. The disappearance of the potato pits threatens to erase generations of handed-down agricultural skills and unique local potato varieties, which are at risk of being lost forever.
summary: Farmers in Gurez, Indian-administered Kashmir, traditionally store harvests underground to survive the Himalayan winter. The fading practice threatens to cause the permanent loss of local potato varieties and generations of handed-down knowledge.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Ofgem to Gain Powers to Fine Energy Executives and Cut Bonuses
content: Exclusive: Ofgem to be given powers to issue fines and rein in bonuses for executives who ‘reward themselves while customers suffer’ Energy bosses in the UK will have their bonuses curtailed when suppliers and brokers break the rules under a crackdown on mis-selling. Through the energy independence bill, which will be introduced on Wednesday, Ofgem will be given new powers to order compensation, impose fines and ban rogue operators that have pushed businesses and households into overpriced contracts.
summary: The energy independence bill, to be introduced on Wednesday, will give Ofgem the authority to issue fines, order compensation, and ban rogue operators involved in mis-selling. It will also allow Ofgem to curb bonuses for energy executives who reward themselves while customers suffer.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Penguin poo accelerates Antarctic snow melt via algal blooms
content:
Researchers have found that penguin guano feeds algal blooms on Antarctic snow, and the algae absorbs significantly more solar energy, accelerating the melt of the ice. The study shows that the presence of these blooms is linked directly to the nutrients deposited by the birds.

As temperatures rise, penguins are moving closer to the South Pole, which could expand this previously unrecognised phenomenon to a wider area of the continent. The shift in penguin distribution may therefore increase the extent of the accelerated melt.

Snow algae are tiny single‑celled plants that thrive in some of the coldest places on Earth. When nutrients are scarce, the algae produces red pigments to protect itself from the sun and slow its growth.
summary: Researchers found that penguins’ guano feeds algal blooms that absorb significantly more solar energy, accelerating Antarctic snow melt. As temperatures rise, penguins are moving closer to the south pole, which could expand this phenomenon to a wider area.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Women and Men Show Similar Short-Term Outcomes After Pulmonary Embolism Thrombectomy
content: New research presented at TCT 2026 found that women and men with intermediate‑risk pulmonary embolism (PE) experience similar short‑term outcomes after aspiration thrombectomy, a catheter‑based procedure that removes blood clots from the lungs. The study noted that women entered treatment with higher pretreatment risk. Results were simultaneously published in JSCAI.
summary: New research presented at TCT 2026 found similar short-term outcomes in women and men with intermediate‑risk pulmonary embolism after aspiration thrombectomy, despite higher pretreatment risk among women. The results were simultaneously published in JSCAI.
author: Medical Xpress

title: AI and HPV testing improve cervical cancer screening in low-resource settings
content: A study led by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal) found that combining HPV testing with artificial intelligence–based image analysis effectively detects precancerous cervical lesions and informs treatment decisions. Conducted within the HPV‑Automated Visual Evaluation (PAVE) Consortium across nine countries, the research was published in The Lancet Obstetrics, Gynaecology & Women’s Health.
summary: Combining HPV testing with AI-based image analysis has shown efficacy in detecting precancerous lesions and guiding treatment decisions. The study, led by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal) and conducted within the HPV-Automated Visual Evaluation (PAVE) Consortium across nine countries, was published in The Lancet Obstetrics, Gynaecology & Women's Health.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Blood signatures may explain half of ultra-processed diet links to heart disease, diabetes
content: A new study by researchers at University College London and Imperial College London has identified two distinct patterns of molecules in the blood that are linked to an ultra‑processed diet and a minimally processed diet. The findings suggest that blood signatures may explain roughly half of the links between ultra‑processed diets and heart disease and diabetes.
summary: Researchers from University College London and Imperial College London identified two distinct blood molecule patterns associated with ultra‑processed and minimally processed diets. The findings suggest these blood signatures may explain roughly half of the links between ultra‑processed diets and heart disease and diabetes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UC San Diego study shows breast milk sugar supports infant gut and prevents jaundice
content: Researchers at the University of California San Diego School of Medicine have published a new study showing that a sugar found in breast milk supports infant gut development and helps prevent hyperbilirubinemia. The condition, in which bilirubin builds up in the blood, causes the yellowing of skin and eyes known as jaundice.
summary: Researchers at the University of California San Diego School of Medicine published a study showing that a sugar in breast milk supports infant gut development. The study also found that this sugar helps prevent hyperbilirubinemia, a condition that causes jaundice.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Single dose of porcine liver nanovesicles reduces alcohol‑induced liver damage in mice
content:
Alcohol‑related liver disease (ALD) is characterized by hepatocellular injury, oxidative stress, inflammation and extracellular matrix remodeling, yet effective therapies remain limited.  

New research published in The American Journal of Pathology found that a single dose of liver matrix‑bound nanovesicles (MBVs) derived from healthy porcine tissue reduced liver injury, fat accumulation and oxidative stress in alcohol‑fed mice, pointing to a possible new therapeutic strategy for ALD.
summary: A single dose of liver matrix‑bound nanovesicles (MBVs) derived from healthy porcine tissue reduced liver injury, fat accumulation, and oxidative stress in alcohol‑fed mice. The study, published in The American Journal of Pathology, suggests a potential new therapeutic strategy for alcohol‑related liver disease.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Hospital-Acquired Anemia Common in ICU Patients, Linked to Poor Outcomes
content: Critically ill patients frequently develop anemia while hospitalized, a condition that can arise even if hemoglobin is low at admission or declines during their stay. The resulting blood loss is linked to a range of adverse patient outcomes, underscoring the importance of monitoring and managing anemia in ICU settings.
summary: Critically ill ICU patients often develop anemia during hospitalization, whether their hemoglobin levels are low upon admission or drop during their stay. This blood loss is linked to a variety of poor patient outcomes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Cannabis Leads Substance-Related Emergency Visits Among Teens and Young Adults
content: A large national study of U.S. emergency department visits and hospitalizations for alcohol or cannabis use found differing age patterns. Among patients presenting for substance‑related problems, cannabis was involved in the majority of visits by adolescents and young adults, whereas alcohol predominated among older adults.
summary: A large national study of emergency department visits and hospitalizations for alcohol or cannabis use found that cannabis was involved in the majority of visits by adolescents and young adults. In contrast, alcohol predominated in visits among older adults.
author: Medical Xpress

title: University of Surrey trial finds multicomponent supplement improves vascular health markers
content: A randomized controlled trial conducted by the University of Surrey found that a multicomponent nutritional supplement improved markers of vascular health. The supplement combined vitamins, minerals, amino acids and plant‑derived bioactives chosen for their relevance to biological processes linked to aging.
summary: A randomized controlled trial led by the University of Surrey found a multicomponent nutritional supplement improved markers of vascular health. The formulation combined vitamins, minerals, amino acids and plant‑derived bioactives selected for relevance to several biological processes associated with aging.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Want more social media engagement? Research suggests changing the message, not your personality
content: New research from Case Western Reserve University indicates that public figures can boost social media engagement by varying their topics and wording. The study suggests that changing the message, rather than the personality, is key to increasing interaction. Specifically, the research highlights the importance of maintaining a consistent psychological voice while diversifying content.
summary: Want more social media engagement? Research suggests changing the message, not your personality.
author: Phys.org

title: Utah study finds climate anxiety widespread among college students
content: College undergraduates are anxious about climate change, many feeling powerless and frustrated about Earth’s future. A new interdisciplinary University of Utah study notes that resources to help students cope are in short supply. The research finds this sentiment extends beyond students studying the environment.
summary: New interdisciplinary University of Utah research indicates that college undergraduates experience significant anxiety and feelings of powerlessness regarding climate change. The study notes that resources to help students cope with these emotions are currently in short supply.
author: Phys.org

title: Researchers Develop Sensors for Continuous Corn Growth Monitoring
content: Researchers have developed sensors capable of continuously monitoring corn growth. These devices allow plant breeders and agronomists to download data from cornstalks and ears, providing specific answers to questions regarding optimal nitrogen application timing and plant responses to various treatments.
summary: Researchers have developed sensors that continuously monitor corn growth, enabling the download of data from cornstalks and ears. This data can help answer questions such as the best time to apply nitrogen and plant responses to fertilizer.
author: Phys.org

title: Researchers Uncover Evidence on Murder of James Starkey, 88 Years Ago
content: Researchers have uncovered compelling new evidence regarding the 1936 murder of British archaeologist James Starkey, who was shot dead while traveling from Lachish to Jerusalem. Archival records now shed light on this 88-year-old mystery, offering explanations for both the identity of the perpetrator and the motive behind the attack.
summary: Pioneering British archaeologist James Starkey was shot dead while traveling from Lachish to Jerusalem eighty-eight years ago. Researchers have uncovered new evidence explaining who was behind his murder and why he was targeted.
author: Phys.org

title: Redfish (Centroberyx affinis) remains
content: One of Australia's most dangerously overfished species, redfish (Centroberyx affinis), will continue to be served on our dinner tables following its latest listing as "conservation dependent." The classification is a loophole allowing species that qualify for critically endangered listings and protections to instead be killed and sold for seafood.
summary: Redfish (Centroberyx affinis) remains.
author: Phys.org

title: KM3NeT tests Lorentz invariance using Mediterranean neutrinos
content:
Scientists are probing whether Einstein’s principle of Lorentz invariance— the idea that the laws of physics are the same everywhere— holds under all conditions. Some theories that try to merge gravity with quantum mechanics suggest that this invariance might break down in extreme environments.

To test this possibility, researchers from the international KM3NeT collaboration examined 5,828 atmospheric neutrino candidate events recorded by the KM3NeT/ORCA neutrino telescope. ORCA is situated deep in the Mediterranean Sea, providing a unique environment for studying neutrinos and the fundamental laws that govern them.
summary: Researchers from the KM3NeT collaboration analyzed 5,828 atmospheric neutrino candidate events detected by the KM3NeT/ORCA telescope. The study aims to investigate whether Lorentz invariance, a core principle of Einstein's theory of relativity, holds universally.
author: Phys.org

title: Children Eating More Ultra-Processed Foods Show Heightened Brain Reward Activity
content:
A new study from the University of Southern California (USC) indicates that ultra-processed foods may impact children’s developing brains in ways that promote weight gain. Researchers examined 46 children aged seven to ten and discovered that those consuming more ultra-processed foods exhibited heightened activity in their brain’s reward system when viewing tempting items such as cookies and French fries.

These intensified neural responses were associated with significant increases in body fat and body mass index (BMI) over the following year. The findings suggest that heightened brain sensitivity to food cues may help explain the link between ultra-processed diets and obesity in children.
summary: Researchers from USC studied 46 children ages 7 to 10 and found that those who ate more ultra-processed foods showed stronger activity in the brain's reward system when viewing tempting foods like cookies and French fries. These heightened brain responses were linked to greater increases in body fat and body mass index one year later.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists develop strategy using tumor CO to make drugs inside cancer cells
content: Scientists have devised a new cancer‑fighting approach that exploits the carbon monoxide produced by tumor cells to generate potent drugs inside the cancer cells themselves. Early laboratory experiments indicate that the method can selectively target cancer cells while sparing healthy tissue, potentially paving the way for safer chemotherapy alternatives.
summary: Scientists have developed a new cancer-fighting strategy that uses carbon monoxide naturally produced by tumor cells to manufacture powerful drugs inside the cancer cells themselves. Early laboratory experiments suggest the technique could selectively attack cancer while sparing healthy cells, potentially paving the way for safer chemotherapy alternatives.
author: Science Daily

title: Gene Editing May Replace Lifelong Meds, but Long-Term Safety Risks Exist
content: Scientists suggest that a single gene‑editing treatment could protect against heart disease, high cholesterol, and other common conditions for decades, potentially replacing lifelong medications. However, they caution that permanently altering genes carries risks that may surface only after many years, making long‑term safety a critical challenge.
summary: A single gene-editing treatment could protect against heart disease, high cholesterol, and other common conditions for decades, potentially replacing lifelong medications. Scientists warn that permanently altering genes introduces risks that could take years to emerge, making long-term safety a critical challenge.
author: Science Daily

title: Hidden Star Siwarha Plows Through Betelgeuse’s Atmosphere, Astronomers Say
content:
Astronomers have identified a hidden companion star, Siwarha, as the source of disturbances in Betelgeuse.  

New radio observations show the smaller star may be plowing through Betelgeuse’s atmosphere, creating disturbances that subtly stretch and distort the red supergiant’s shape.
summary: Astronomers have identified a hidden companion star named Siwarha as the cause of disturbances in Betelgeuse’s atmosphere. New radio observations show the smaller star may be plowing through Betelgeuse’s enormous atmosphere, subtly stretching and distorting the red supergiant’s shape.
author: Science Daily

title: Varda Space Industries Launches Three Capsules to Grow Cancer Drug Crystals in Orbit
content:
California‑based Varda Space Industries has placed three washing‑machine‑sized capsules 300 miles above Earth to test the production of pharmaceutical materials in microgravity. Inside one capsule, researchers are growing tiny crystals of a potential cancer drug, while the other two are evaluating heat‑shield materials and navigation systems needed for the capsules’ return to Earth at hypersonic speeds.  

The company launched the first two capsules on 1 October and added a third on 20 October, creating the first instance of three spacecraft operating simultaneously in orbit. The experiments represent a modest yet significant step toward Varda’s goal of establishing a fleet of orbiting pharmaceutical factories.  

By demonstrating the feasibility of drug crystal growth and reentry technology in space, Varda is moving closer to a new industry that could manufacture drugs and other high‑value materials beyond Earth’s atmosphere.
summary: Three Varda Space Industries capsules are orbiting 300 miles above Earth, with one growing crystals of a potential cancer drug in microgravity. The other two are testing heat protection materials and navigation systems for reentry, marking the first time the company has three spacecraft simultaneously in orbit.
author: Guardian Science

title: Bird flu raging on Utah mink farm, officials take little action
content: Mink farms are the perfect petri dishes for deadly flu strains to emerge. Yet officials appear to be protecting business interests over human lives Could this be ground zero? Could it be the spot where the next pandemic begins? It’s certainly a candidate, not least because the chain of events that could trigger a plague far worse than Covid-19 looks like the opening sequence of a disaster movie. A really bad disaster movie, in which the levels of carelessness and turpitude defy belief. A report by the investigative news service ProPublica reveals that bird flu has been raging in a mink farm in Utah since August, and it appears next to nothing has been done by public officials. In 2023, I warned in the Guardian that mink farms could scarcely be better designed to generate lethal plagues. This is for three reasons: mink are fed on the offcuts of chickens, cows and other farm animals, in which new viral variants often develop; mink readily host both avian and human flu viruses, which can then exchange genetic material, turning a bird disease into a human one; and mink possess extremely high “zoonotic potential” – the ability to infect animals of other species, including human beings. George Monbiot is a Guardian columnist
summary: ProPublica reports that bird flu has been circulating in a mink farm in Utah since August. Public officials appear to have taken little action to address the outbreak.
author: Guardian Science

title: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory to re-enter atmosphere Wednesday after failed rescue
content: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, a telescope launched in 2004, is slated to re‑enter Earth’s atmosphere on Wednesday, where it will burn up. The satellite, which has spent two decades observing the most powerful cosmic explosions, was originally built to operate its three telescopes for only two years. It can no longer steer or conduct observations, and its re‑entry will be uncontrolled. A rescue attempt for the aging spacecraft was made but was unsuccessful, leading to the current uncontrolled plunge.
summary: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, which has spent two decades studying cosmic explosions, is expected to re-enter Earth’s atmosphere on Wednesday and burn up. The satellite, designed for a two‑year mission, can no longer steer or observe and its re‑entry will be uncontrolled.
author: Guardian Science

title: Before the Dawn in America’s Heartland
content:
On October 18, 2026, clear skies over much of the eastern United States allowed an astronaut aboard the International Space Station to capture a wide-angle photograph of the region during predawn hours. The image, taken at 4:54 a.m. Central Daylight Time (09:54 Universal Time), displays illuminated cities of various sizes arrayed across the darkened landscape. Major metropolitan areas in the U.S. Midwest, including Chicago, Illinois, and Detroit, Michigan, appear as some of the brightest features in the scene. Mid-sized cities such as Indianapolis, Indiana; Cincinnati, Ohio; and Louisville, Kentucky, also shine brightly, with their interconnections along state and interstate highways clearly visible.

Above the network of nighttime lights and Earth’s lower atmosphere, a diffuse layer of green and orange airglow is visible along the horizon to the left. This band of light is produced when sunlight strikes atoms and molecules in the upper atmosphere, causing them to eject photons. To the right, light from the Sun arcs across the horizon, indicating that sunrise was approximately one hour away on the East Coast and about two hours away in Chicago. The specific photograph, identified as ISS075-E-226709, was acquired using a Nikon Z9 digital camera with a 14-millimeter focal length by a member of the Expedition 75 crew.

Astronaut photographs and other remote sensing observations of nighttime lights are scientifically valuable for tracking changes in the built environment. While the wide view shows Chicago’s lightscape as a homogeneous pale yellow, detailed photography reveals a range of colors stemming from different types of lighting. Researchers utilizing NASA’s Gateway to Astronaut Photography of Earth archive have developed methods to distinguish these lighting types within image pixels. Systematically quantifying the brightness, color, and extent of urban lights provides insight into how cities grow and evolve.

Satellite sensors also contribute to monitoring these changes. NASA’s Black Marble nighttime lights product suite uses satellite observations to generate science-quality records of global nighttime lights at daily, monthly, and yearly time scales. In the eastern United States, scientists have employed these data to track events such as power outages and restorations following major storms, lighting changes associated with new infrastructure, and transitions from older lighting forms to LED lighting.

The images presented are provided by the ISS Crew Earth Observations Facility and the Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit at NASA Johnson Space Center. The International Space Station Program supports this laboratory as part of the ISS National Lab to ensure astronauts capture images of Earth that are of high value to scientists and the public, making them freely available on the internet. The story was written by Lindsey Doermann, and additional images taken by astronauts and cosmonauts can be viewed through the NASA/JSC Gateway to Astronaut Photography of Earth.
summary: Before the Dawn in America’s Heartland.
author: NASA News

title: APOD November 4, 2026 features IC 342, the Not‑So‑Hidden Galaxy
content: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 4 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. The Not-So-Hidden Galaxy, IC 342 Explanation: “I see” IC 342, the Hidden Galaxy! Today’s image peers through the plane of the Milky Way, through all its gas, dust and stars, to unveil this spiral galaxy. IC 342 (or Caldwell 5 ) is one of the brightest members of the IC 342/ Maffei group of galaxies. Located about 10 million light years away, this group is quite close to the Local Group that includes our Milky Way. Inaccurate accounting of the crowded and dusty Milky Way foreground has led to misunderstandings in IC 342’s history, including the theory that the galaxy was ejected from the Local Group. IC 342 has its own dust intermittently blocking the glow of hydrogen gas, indicating the presence of bright, young stars. Magnetic field maps of IC 342 reveal that magnetic fields may contribute substantially to one of the biggest galactic puzzles: how do spiral arms form? title: Show HN: Uncracked City detective game lets players question lying LLM suspects
content: To give you some context on the project. I'm a solo founder and I use AI heavily in my work. The idea came from wanting players to discover cities. Each city has its own history, so every case is set in a real city with real public places. The crime and the people are on other hand invented. The part that I care most is the playable aspect of the game, a model plays the detective and must solve the case before it goes live. As of today: it's free on Android, the iOS version is still waiting to be reviewed by Apple. It's available in six popular languages, but adding more languages is just a matter of time and demand. My long term vision if it takes off: weekly cases, private parties like a team-building escape game, an MCP so a game master can build their own scenario from ChatGPT or Claude, and maybe tourism offices since players travel the world. Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50358352 Points: 22 # Comments: 9
summary: Uncracked City is a solo‑founder detective game that uses AI to let a model interrogate LLM suspects who lie, with each case set in a real city. The game is free on Android, pending iOS review, and currently supports six languages.

title: Nexus Mods requires AI use disclosure for all new mod uploads
content:
Nexus Mods announced that AI usage disclosure will be mandatory for new mod uploads. Mod authors must declare whether AI has been used. This announcement is part of a larger post about AI‑generated content on the platform.  

The post, written by site owner Victor “Foledinho” Folmann, notes that a common concern is unclear disclosure of AI use. Nexus Mods already uses tags for AI‑generated and AI‑assisted mods, but the site acknowledges there is room to improve accessibility and clarity of that information.
summary: Nexus Mods announced that mod authors must declare whether AI was used when uploading new mods. Site owner Victor "Foledinho" Folmann said the policy builds on existing AI-generated and AI-assisted tags to make such information clearer.

title: Nintendo to release Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Nov 5
content:
Nintendo announced a remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the upcoming Switch 2 console. The new version arrives 28 years after the original Nintendo 64 launch and features a more realistic visual style, a jump button, a sprint option, full voice acting, and a “Threads of Time” tool that helps players track their progress. While the presentation is updated, many elements are expected to stay faithful to the classic N64 release.

To coincide with the remake, Nintendo released a special edition Switch 2 console and Switch 2 Pro Controller adorned with Triforce imagery. The game is slated for release on November 5. A preorder promotion offers a $10 discount for one week, and Nintendo has provided an overview trailer as part of its coverage. Additional related items include Hori’s electronic Ocarina of Time, which the announcement notes requires no musical talent.
summary: Nintendo to release Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Nov 5.
author: The Verge

title: AMD posts record $13.4B revenue as data center drives largest quarter
content: AMD CEO Lisa Su said in the company's quarterly earnings call on Tuesday that Q3 2026 was "was the largest and most profitable in our history." AMD reported a record $13.4 billion in quarterly revenue, and it's predicting it will hit another record high next quarter of $17 billion. The company's data center business is driving that growth, with $8.5 billion in data center quarterly revenue for Q3 2026. Su said AMD's expecting its revenue to "grow more than 80 percent in 2027," adding that "data center will be the largest contributor." Eventually, most of AMD's revenue might come from its data center business. In response to a question durin …
summary: AMD posts record $13.4B revenue as data center drives largest quarter.

content: The TechCrunch Founder Summit will be held in Boston, and pass prices are set to rise tomorrow at 9 a.m. ET. Attendees can lock in savings of up to $100 on a pass and receive a second pass for free if they purchase before the price increase.

title: AI pioneer Geoffrey Hinton warns technology could cause major power or banking blackout
content: Nobel winner warns the tech could be near to triggering major incident such as power or banking shutdown One of the “godfathers of AI”, Geoffrey Hinton, has said it could turn out that humans would have been better off never developing the technology as he warned it could trigger a large-scale incident this year or next, such as a temporary blackout of financial or power systems. The Nobel prize-winning computer scientist told the Guardian he is not a “doomer” about the technology that is underpinned by his groundbreaking research into artificial neural networks and believes AI has the potential to lead to a “wonderful future” but he said “it might be that we would have been better off never developing it”.
summary: AI pioneer Geoffrey Hinton warns technology could cause major power or banking blackout.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Canva to cut or relocate over 1,200 jobs in major restructure
content:
Canva has announced a major restructure that will cut or relocate more than 1,200 employees, amounting to 22 % of its global workforce. Chief executive Melanie Perkins described the decision as “without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen‑year history” in an email to staff.

The layoffs target staff who helped build the Australian‑founded design platform, reflecting a broader trend in the technology sector. Software companies are reshaping their operations to remain competitive against cheaper artificial‑intelligence disruptors while integrating AI tools into their own products.
summary: Canva is cutting or relocating more than 1,200 jobs, about 22% of its global workforce, as part of a major restructure. Chief executive Melanie Perkins said the cuts are the hardest moment in the company's thirteen‑year history in an email to staff.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Democrats seize control of US Congress after long night for Republican party
content: Democrats have seized control of the U.S. Congress, an outcome described as a long night for the Republican Party. The shift would give Democrats a significant check on Trump, potentially enabling investigations of his administration and increasing pressure on the White House over its policies.
summary: Democrats have seized control of the US Congress. The new majority would give Democrats a significant check on Trump and could allow them to investigate his administration and increase pressure on the White House over its policies.
author: Euronews

title: Black female governor, gay male senator, Native American female governor win midterms
content: In the recent midterm election, voters elected the first Black female governor, the first openly gay male senator and the first female Native American governor, marking historic leadership firsts for minorities across the United States. The outcomes contributed to a broader sweep of resounding wins for Democrats.
summary: The first Black female governor, the first openly gay male senator and the first female Native American governor were elected in the midterm vote. The elections contributed to a series of resounding wins for Democrats.

title: Democrat James Talarico projected winner of Texas US Senate race
content: Democrat James Talarico has won the US Senate race in Texas, according to US media projections, marking a major breakthrough in a traditionally Republican state.
summary: Democrat James Talarico has won the US Senate race in Texas, according to US media projections. The result is described as a major breakthrough in a traditionally Republican state.

title: Democrats flip Republican Senate seat and make House inroads in Tuesday midterms
content: Democrats secured early victories in Tuesday's US midterm elections, flipping a Republican-held Senate seat and making inroads in conservative House districts. These results presented President Donald Trump with the prospect of a significant election setback. France 24's Douglas Herbert provided analysis of the developing situation.
summary: Democrats notched a string of early victories in US midterm elections Tuesday, flipping a Republican-held Senate seat. They also made inroads in conservative House districts as President Donald Trump faced a bruising election setback.

title: US polls show significant swing toward Democrats even in areas they didn’t win
content: Tens of millions of Americans cast their vote in the crucial polls that have been pitched as a referendum on Donald Trump's presidency amid anger at surging petrol prices, tariffs and the Iran war. We discuss the first results with France 24's Kethevane Gorjestani and Fraser Jackson. "Even in places where the Democrats haven't won, the swing towards them has been significant", he says.
summary: Tens of millions of Americans voted in polls framed as a referendum on Donald Trump’s presidency amid anger over rising petrol prices, tariffs and the Iran war. Analysts said the swing toward Democrats was significant even in places they did not win.
author: France 24

title: Ipsos Senior VP Mallory Newall says voters increasingly frustrated with Trump amid midterms
content: The polls in these midterm elections suggest that "this will either be a good night or a historic night for Democrats". But what is driving this momentum? We discuss this with our guest, Mallory Newall, Senior Vice President at Ipsos. "We've seen in our polling at Ipsos in recent weeks and months that voters have become increasingly frustrated with President Trump," she says.
summary: Polls for the US midterm elections suggest the result could be a good night or a historic night for Democrats. Mallory Newall, Senior Vice President at Ipsos, said voters have become increasingly frustrated with President Trump.

title: Democrats secure Senate control with wins in Texas, Iowa and other states
content: Democrats secured control of the U.S. Senate in the midterm elections held on Tuesday. Initial results indicated the party won key races in Texas, Ohio, North Carolina, South Carolina, Kansas, and Iowa. The victories in Texas and Iowa were highlighted as particularly surprising by election analysts.
