author: MIT Tech Review

title: Binance Reports $6.34B Hack by North Korean Attackers Using Fake Interview
content: Binance reported that a suspected North Korean hacking group carried out a $6.34 billion theft from its systems. The attackers deceived an engineer with a fake job interview and a malicious download, which allowed them to gain a foothold and steal billions, according to the company.
summary: Suspected North Korean attackers duped a Binance engineer with a fake job interview and a malicious download. The intrusion gave them a foothold in Binance’s system and allowed them to steal billions, according to Binance.
author: Wired

title: Xbox Nano Controller to Connect Directly to Cloud Gaming Over Wi-Fi
content:
Microsoft will release its new Xbox Nano controller tomorrow.  The device contains a hidden feature that lets it connect directly to Xbox Cloud Gaming over Wi‑Fi, a capability that has not yet been officially announced.

The direct‑cloud connection is intended to reduce latency, mirroring the approach used by Google’s Stadia controllers.  Microsoft is privately testing the feature on the new Xbox Cloud Gaming website, and it will require users to pair the Nano controller over Wi‑Fi with Microsoft’s cloud servers.
summary: Microsoft is about to launch its new Xbox Nano controller tomorrow. The Nano can connect directly to Xbox Cloud Gaming over Wi-Fi to improve latency, a feature still privately tested.
author: The Verge

title: Moft Unveils Dynamic Folio Case for iPhone Duo with Kickstand and Grip
content:
Moft has re‑engineered its Dynamic Folio, originally launched in early 2025 for the iPad, into a new case for Apple’s iPhone Duo. The updated design adds a kickstand that lets the Duo rest at multiple angles for hands‑free use, and its origami‑style screen cover can double as a finger grip while holding the phone.  

The Dynamic Folio Case for iPhone Duo is available for preorder on Moft’s online store at $89.99. Buyers can choose navy blue, misty cove, or sapphire. Shipping is slated to begin in mid‑December, and the price represents a modest increase over Moft’s earlier offering.
summary: Moft has redesigned its Dynamic Folio as a case for the iPhone Duo that can be used as a kickstand and finger grip. The case is available for preorder at $89.99 in navy blue, misty cove, and sapphire, with shipping expected to start in mid December.
author: The Verge

title: Netflix Adds AI Discover Tab to Show Theme‑Based Recommendations
content:
Netflix is introducing a new "AI Discover" tab to its TV app, featuring experimental, AI-powered tools designed to assist users in finding new content. The initial experiment presents thematic categories such as "Something Light," "Family Movie Night," and "Quick Watches." Selecting a theme generates corresponding show and movie recommendations tailored to that specific mood or occasion.

The platform allows users to provide feedback on these suggestions, with the app retaining negative responses to refine future picks. Netflix states that AI Discover operates on a new intelligence layer built to respond to member input in real time while continuously learning from user interactions.
summary: Netflix’s TV app will feature a new “AI Discover” tab that surfaces experimental, AI‑powered recommendations. The tab offers theme‑based suggestions such as “Something Light” and “Family Movie Night,” and learns from user feedback in real time.
author: The Verge

title: Google Home Speaker with Gemini AI drops to $79, 20% off at major retailers
content:
Google’s newest Home Speaker, powered by the Gemini AI model, is now being offered at a discount of roughly 20 percent. The device, which launched in June, is listed for $79—down from its regular $99.99 price—at major retailers including Best Buy, Walmart and Target, and is available in four color options.

The speaker’s design has been highlighted for its compact size, which is smaller than the previous‑generation Nest Audio, making it easy to place in various rooms. Reviewers noted that despite its reduced footprint the unit delivers loud, clear 360‑degree audio, and in comparative testing it sounded cleaner and sharper than the similarly priced Amazon Echo Dot Max, though some reviewers preferred the Echo’s fuller bass. The older Nest Audio is still regarded as having superior overall sound, but the new model offers a lower price and smaller size.

In addition to audio performance, the Google Home Speaker supports the Matter standard and includes a Thread border router, enabling control of a broad range of compatible smart‑home devices. It can also serve as an audio output for the Google TV Streamer 4K, allowing TV sound to be played through one or two speakers instead of the TV’s built‑in speakers.

A key feature of the device is its Gemini‑based assistant, which is described as more adept at natural‑language and complex requests than the earlier Google Assistant. Reviewers observed that Gemini can handle multiple smart‑home commands simultaneously and respond to conversational prompts, such as adjusting the air conditioner when a temperature complaint is mentioned. Some Gemini capabilities, including “Gemini Live” for extended conversations without repeating the wake word, require a $10‑per‑month Google Home Premium subscription.
summary: We’re big fans of the Google Home Speaker’s design. | Photo: Jennifer Patison Tuohy / The Verge If you’re looking for a good smart speaker, the Google Home Speaker is down to around $79 ($20 off) in all four colors at Best Buy, Walmart, and Target.
author: The Verge

title: Steam approval delays cause indie game Food Devils to miss planned launch
content:
Indie developers are reporting that Steam’s approval process is causing unexpected delays, leading some games to miss their scheduled launch dates. A screenshot of the upcoming title Food Devils shows the game listed as missing its planned release today. The developer, Studio Daimon, submitted the game’s build to Steam on October 12 and intended to launch in early access on the same day.

According to a post by game director Alfred Kamon, the build is “still awaiting approval,” and the team does not know when Steam will grant final clearance. Kamon noted that the studio sent an additional support ticket last week to inquire about the situation. Other indie developers have similarly posted on social media about unusually long wait times for Steam’s game‑submission approvals.
summary: Indie developers have posted about unusually long Steam approval wait times that are causing missed launch dates. Studio Daimon's title Food Devils, submitted on October 12, remained awaiting approval on its scheduled early‑access launch day, with director Alfred Kamon saying Steam has not yet given final OK.
author: The Verge

title: Reddit tests ads in search results
content:
Reddit is expanding its advertising program by testing ads in the platform’s search results. The company says the ads will be placed “based on a range of factors, including contextual relevance to a search query,” so a query such as “espresso station” could show ads for espresso products, while “home office setup” might display ads for monitors, desks or chairs.  

Reddit already serves ads across its feeds in formats that include images, videos, sponsored posts, AMAs and within discussion threads. The new search‑based placement is part of a broader set of platform changes announced by Reddit.
summary: Reddit is testing ads that appear within its search results based on factors such as contextual relevance to a query. The platform already shows ads across feeds, threads and in formats including images, videos, sponsored posts and AMAs.
author: The Verge

title: OpenAI says ChatGPT queries now equal 20% of Google searches
content:
OpenAI announced that the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google. The statement was made by Adam Fry, OpenAI’s consumer product lead for ChatGPT, at a press event on Monday.  

Fry explained that OpenAI defines a “search” as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, distinguishing it from tasks such as defining a term or providing a simple how‑to explanation.  

He did not disclose the source of the Google search‑volume figure. Despite matching one‑fifth of Google’s search traffic, OpenAI noted that this level is still a long way from overtaking the search‑engine giant.
summary: OpenAI announced that the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google. The announcement was made by Adam Fry, OpenAI's consumer product lead for ChatGPT, at a press event on Monday.
author: The Verge

title: Apple watchOS 27.3 beta adds always‑on Audio Intelligence with Siri Recap and Live Rewind
content:
Apple has begun rolling out the watchOS 27.3 developer beta, which adds always‑on Audio Intelligence capabilities to the Apple Watch. The update enables Siri to access the watch’s microphone and introduces two features: Siri Recap, which uses ambient listening to create conversation summaries, and Live Rewind, which provides text transcripts of the most recent 15 seconds of detected audio.

In the same release, Apple is making a redesigned Health app available for testing in the iOS 27.3 developer beta and has announced expanded language support that includes global English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, French, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish and Turkish.
summary: Apple watchOS 27.3 beta adds always‑on Audio Intelligence with Siri Recap and Live Rewind.
author: The Verge

title: Mercedes-Benz develops holographic heads-up display for car interiors
content:
Mercedes‑Benz arranged for a representative from Ars to travel from Los Angeles to Stuttgart, Germany, and provided accommodation so the outlet could experience the company’s new holographic display. The article notes that Ars does not accept paid editorial content.

The piece places the holographic display in the context of an increasing number of screens in luxury car interiors, describing how screens have grown larger, multiplied across dashboards and taken on new forms. It questions whether consumers actually desire more screens and observes that premium features eventually filter down to mainstream vehicles, limiting how large screens can become.

Mercedes‑Benz’s holographic display is presented as a next‑step alternative to traditional screens. Described as a more advanced form of heads‑up display (HUD), it aims to move beyond conventional visual interfaces without invoking science‑fiction imagery. The article invites readers to view the full story for additional details.
summary: Mercedes-Benz is working on a new holographic display, described as a more advanced form of heads-up display. The company provided flights from Los Angeles to Stuttgart, Germany, and accommodation so Ars could experience the technology.
author: Ars Technica

title: EPA ends 20-year effort to monitor factory farm air pollution
content:
The Environmental Protection Agency announced late last week that it will end a more‑than‑20‑year effort to develop methods for monitoring air pollution from factory farms. The agency said the decision effectively halts its attempts to regulate these facilities under the Clean Air Act.

The announcement, made just days before the midterm elections, was described by the EPA as a long‑awaited reprieve for farmers, a constituency the agency noted as historically important to former President Trump and the Republican Party.

Factory farms house tens of thousands of animals in confined spaces, and the agency’s statement noted that waste can be released through ventilation fans or from large lagoons of liquid effluent. Such livestock operations emit fine particulate matter, ammonia, nitrogen oxides, sulfur dioxide and volatile organic compounds, a mix the agency said contributes to air pollution. Research cited in the release linked emissions from these operations to nearly 12,700 deaths annually in the United States.
summary: EPA ends 20-year effort to monitor factory farm air pollution.
author: Ars Technica

title: Meta temporarily suspends No Kings Instagram account during early voting push
content:
Over the weekend, the No Kings Coalition reported that Meta declined to commit to measures that would prevent automated systems from suspending one of Instagram’s most prominent pro‑democracy accounts if activity around the page surged during the midterm elections. The coalition’s demand followed Meta’s apology for temporarily suspending the No Kings Instagram account and disabling access for four hours during a peak period of an early‑voting push by the group.

In a post on X, Meta’s Andy Stone explained that the account had been using a Claude AI tool in a manner that made it appear to be a bot. Stone said automated review detected the error within an hour, but additional hurdles kept administrators locked out of the account. State and federal lawmakers, as well as a coalition of 14 attorneys general, have asked Meta to provide a fuller explanation of its actions.

Meta responded by offering a meeting with a technical expert to clarify the mistake, but the No Kings Coalition rejected that proposal. The group requested a meeting with Meta senior leadership instead, arguing that the issue extends beyond its Instagram account and that Americans need assurance that voting content will not be suppressed ahead of or on election day. Among eight questions, the coalition asked Meta to publicly disclose any communications with the Trump administration regarding the No Kings account or the historic early‑voting day event.
summary: Meta apologized after temporarily suspending the No Kings Instagram account and disabling access for four hours during an early‑voting push. The No Kings Coalition rejected Meta’s offer of a technical‑expert meeting, demanding senior leadership talks and disclosure of any communications with the Trump administration, while lawmakers and 14 attorneys general have asked for further explanation.
author: Ars Technica

title: UEFI bootkit BlackLotus infects fully patched Windows 11 systems
content:
In 2023 researchers documented a malware family called BlackLotus, the first publicly observed UEFI bootkit capable of bypassing Secure Boot on fully updated Windows 11 systems. By subverting the industry‑wide chain‑of‑trust mechanism, the bootkit was able to execute malicious code before the operating system and its security defenses were fully loaded.

Microsoft had already released a patch for the vulnerability exploited by BlackLotus in 2022. Subsequent updates in 2023 and 2024 added a new certificate that no longer trusted the vulnerable boot managers and introduced a method to revoke trust in the digital certificate used to sign older vulnerable Windows boot managers.

Despite these mitigations, a later variant tracked as BlackX infected organizations that had applied all of the aforementioned patches. The article notes that the infected systems had the full set of updates, prompting questions about how the bootkit succeeded despite the existing protections. A brief overview of UEFI’s role in initializing hardware and loading the OS is also provided.
summary: In 2023, malware tracked as BlackLotus became the first publicly documented in‑the‑wild UEFI bootkit capable of bypassing Secure Boot on fully updated Windows 11 computers. The organizations infected by the newer bootkit, tracked as BlackX, had installed Microsoft’s 2022 patch and the 2023‑2024 updates that added a new certificate and revocation capability.
author: Ars Technica

title: Argo Space bets its future on water propulsion for in‑space travel
content:
Three engineers who spent the Falcon 9 era at SpaceX—Robert, Ryan and Kirby Carlisle—have left the company to pursue a new venture in space. After working on launching, refurbishing and selling rockets, the brothers decided to focus on spacecraft rather than rockets when they founded their own firm.

In late 2022 the Carlisle brothers established Argo Space, a company aimed at building infrastructure in orbit. Their stated goal is to enable in‑space transportation without relying on propellants launched from Earth. To that end, Argo Space has selected water as its propulsion medium, citing its potential to be harvested on the Moon and its abundance throughout the Solar System.
summary: The Carlisle brothers—Robert, Ryan and Kirby—who worked at SpaceX during the Falcon 9 era founded Argo Space in late 2022 to build space infrastructure. The company plans to use water, harvestable on the Moon and abundant throughout the Solar System, as a propellant to eliminate the need for Earth‑sourced fuel.
author: Ars Technica

title: Google shuts down x. Cpe botnet affecting 1.3 million Android TV boxes
content:
Google’s Threat Intelligence Group announced that it has dismantled a large botnet known as x. Cpe.  The network operated on more than 1.3 million Android TV devices that had been certified by Google, and it was traced to boxes manufactured by Shenzhen‑based Videostrong Technology.  According to the group’s blog post, the malware used obfuscation techniques that allowed it to bypass Google’s certification screening.

The compromised devices, most of which were sold under the MECOOL brand, contained a backdoor that let the attacker install the botnet after the boxes were set up and connected online.  A stub application identified as x. Cpe or com. Oemservice phoned home, held system‑level permissions, and could install additional malware modules while disabling Play Protect, which would otherwise flag the packages as malicious.  The botnet evolved from a single‑stage dropper into a modular three‑stage platform that offered access to third parties.
summary: Google's Threat Intelligence Group says it has shut down a massive botnet called x. Cpe.
author: Ars Technica

title: Google lets schools disable AI tools, but they lose access to Search
content: Google is offering schools the option to turn off its AI tools. However, the company notes that schools that choose to block AI entirely will also lose access to Google Search, because AI features are now built into the search engine.
summary: Google will let schools disable its AI tools. Schools that restrict AI will no longer be able to use Google Search because AI features are now integrated into the search engine.
author: TechCrunch

title: Binance fights brand damage after record $6.3bn crypto hack
content:
The world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance, is confronting a wave of angry customers after a record‑breaking hack that cost roughly $6.3 billion. The incident has sparked a brand‑recovery effort as the platform seeks to manage the fallout and restore user confidence.

The discussion of the hack appears in TechScape, a newsletter that examines how technology shapes daily life. The current issue highlights the Binance breach alongside other tech‑related topics, and invites readers to share whether they have been affected by the incident.
summary: Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, is facing fallout from a record $6.3 billion hack and angry customers. The company is working to protect its brand after the breach.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Qatar sees hope for US-Iran interim deal despite fresh US strikes
content: Qatar said on Tuesday that it sees hope for an interim U.S.–Iran agreement as mediators continue to exchange proposals in real time. The statement noted that fresh U.S. strikes and ongoing threats to shipping through the Hormuz Strait are complicating efforts to end the Iran war.
summary: Qatar said Tuesday it saw hope for an interim deal as mediators continue to exchange proposals. Fresh US strikes and threats to shipping through Hormuz continue to complicate efforts to end the Iran war.
author: Euronews

title: South Korea and Turkey sign financing pact to fund nuclear projects, including Sinop plant
content: Turkey and South Korea have signed a financing agreement that explores funding for nuclear projects, reflecting an expansion of nuclear, defence and trade ties between the two nations. Ankara is weighing potential partners for its planned Sinop nuclear power plant, with Seoul seeking a role in the project.
summary: Turkey and South Korea are expanding nuclear, defence and trade ties. Their latest agreement explores funding for nuclear projects, while Ankara weighs potential partners for its planned Sinop plant.
author: Euronews

title: Americans vote in midterms that will decide Congress control for Trump's final two years
content: Voters are casting ballots in Fairfax, Virginia, and in New York as Americans head to the polls for the midterm elections. These elections will decide which party controls Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term.
summary: Voters cast ballots in Fairfax, Virginia, and New York. The midterm elections will determine control of Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term.
author: Euronews

title: Senate races in unexpected Republican states will decide midterm control
content: Democrats appear poised to secure the U.S. House, while control of the Senate hinges on a few competitive races in states that Republicans had not anticipated needing to defend. Those contests will determine which party holds the Senate after the midterm elections.
summary: Democrats look all but certain to take the US House. The real fight is for the Senate, where a handful of races in states Republicans never expected to defend will decide who controls Washington.
author: Euronews

title: James Talarico leads polls in Texas Senate race aiming to end Democrats' 30-year streak
content: Democratic candidate James Talarico is currently leading the polls in Texas ahead of the U.S. Senate race against Republican Ken Paxton. The contest is among the most closely watched midterm battles, as Democrats aim to end a 30‑year losing streak in the state. The story is reported by Andrés Espinal from Austin, Texas.
summary: In Texas, Democratic candidate James Talarico is leading the polls ahead of a high-stakes US Senate race against Republican Ken Paxton. The contest is one of the most closely watched battles of the midterm elections, with Democrats hoping to end a 30-year losing streak in the state.
author: France 24

title: US Midterm Elections: Over 58 Million Americans Cast Early Ballots
content:
Over 58 million Americans have already cast early ballots for the U.S. midterm elections, a figure that underscores the high level of voter participation ahead of the vote.  

Pollsters have framed the election as a referendum on President Donald Trump, with polls opening in dozens of states to gauge his influence. The prevailing sentiment in those polls is that Democrats are poised to regain the House of Representatives.  

However, the same polls raise the question of whether Democrats could also capture the Senate, potentially blocking Trump’s agenda during his final two years in office.
summary: Polls have opened in dozens of states as a referendum on US President Donald Trump, with most suggesting Democrats will retake the House of Representatives. The Senate outcome could stymie Trump's agenda in his final two years in office.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine's Operation Veles sends troops into disused pipeline in Kupiansk
content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky praised the success of Operation Veles, in which Kyiv forces entered a disused gas pipeline in the Kupiansk region to confront Russian troops. Russian units have employed underground tactics for over two years to bypass Ukrainian lines, a method Kyiv now adopts as a new battlefield strategy.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Operation Veles succeeded as Kyiv troops moved deep into a disused gas pipeline in the Kupiansk region to confront Russian troops. Russian forces have used underground tactics for more than two years to slip past Ukrainian lines, giving Kyiv a new battlefield strategy.
author: France 24

title: Russian households see utility bills rise over 50% as Ukraine war drags
content: Russian households are experiencing growing financial pressure as Moscow’s strikes continue across Ukraine and the country contends with drone attacks from Ukraine. Since the war began in 2022, utility bills in Russia have risen by more than 50%, including an increase of over 13% in the current year.
summary: Russian citizens are facing increasing financial strain as Moscow continues strikes across Ukraine. Since the start of the war in 2022, utility bills in Russia have risen by more than 50%, including over 13% this year, amid ongoing drone attacks originating from Ukraine.
author: France 24

title: Democrats plan investigations of Trump administration if they regain congressional control
content: Democrats are preparing to launch a series of investigations into President Donald Trump’s administration and business dealings should they regain control of one or both chambers of Congress. They are devising strategies to bypass White House obstruction and avoid the impeachment deadlock that plagued the legislature during Trump’s first term.
summary: Democrats are preparing to launch a flurry of investigations into President Donald Trump’s administration and business dealings if they retake one or both chambers of Congress. They are devising strategies to circumvent White House obstruction and avoid the impeachment deadlock that consumed the legislature during Trump’s first term.
author: France 24

title: France's dermatologist shortage deepens as half near retirement, only 100 trained yearly
content:
Around 200,000 cases of skin cancer are diagnosed in France every year, yet the country is facing a growing difficulty in securing dermatology appointments. Half of France’s dermatologists are nearing retirement, and only about 100 new specialists are trained each year, creating a widening gap between demand and supply.

The shortage has prompted some professionals to devise innovative solutions to address the crisis. According to a report by FRANCE 24’s Aurore Dupuis and Sonia Baritello, these new approaches aim to improve access to dermatological care amid the mounting shortage.
summary: Around 200,000 skin‑cancer cases are diagnosed in France each year, but patients are finding dermatologist appointments increasingly difficult to secure. Half of the country’s dermatologists are nearing retirement and only about 100 new specialists are trained annually, prompting some to seek innovative solutions.
author: France 24

title: Democrats target retaking one or both chambers in US midterm elections
content: Will it be a trickle, a wave, or a tsunami? Election Day in the United States with Democrats hoping to take back one or both houses of Congress. We’ll track the turnout, gauge the mood and raise the curtain ahead of Midterms results that are sure to shape the last two years of Donald Trump’s second and final term. Will a US president who’s already broken norms with his maximum use of executive powers be affected by the results a little, a lot, or not at all?
summary: Democrats are hoping to take back one or both houses of Congress in the upcoming US midterm elections. The elections will take place during Donald Trump’s second term.
author: France 24

title: US voters elect new Congress in midterm election, impacting future and Trump’s legacy
content: US voters are electing a new Congress in the midterm election. According to the source, the outcome will be decisive for the United States’ future and will serve as a judgment on Donald Trump’s second term as president.
summary: US voters are electing a new Congress in the midterm election. The outcome will be decisive for the United States’ future and will serve as a judgment on Donald Trump’s second term as president.
author: DW World

title: US tech giants issue AI bonds, pressuring France, Germany, Italy bond markets
content: France, Germany and Italy are confronting a volatile bond market as war‑related inflation pressures intensify. At the same time, U.S. technology companies are issuing billions of dollars in AI‑linked bonds, entering the same investor space as the cash‑strained European governments and creating additional competition for funding.
summary: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. US tech giants are now issuing billions in AI bonds, competing with cash-strapped European governments.
author: DW World

title: US Midterm Election's Effect on Trump's Iran Policy Unclear
content: The United States’ upcoming midterm elections are approaching, yet analysts note that their effect on the ongoing Iran conflict is uncertain. They add that Washington’s political elite may be more unified on Iran policy than public perception suggests.

content: Intensified fighting between Iran‑backed Houthi rebels and Yemeni government forces around Taiz has left residents in a state of panic. The clashes have triggered shortages of food, water and medical supplies, and thousands of people have fled their homes.

title: Philippe Jaenada wins Prix Goncourt for true‑crime novel on 1949 Paris murder
content:
Philippe Jaenada was announced on Tuesday afternoon as the winner of France’s most prestigious literary prize, the Prix Goncourt. The award was given for his novel L’Inconnue du quai de Javel (The Unknown Woman of the Quai de Javel).

The novel is a true‑crime investigation that attempts to solve a 77‑year‑old cold case. It focuses on the murder of a 29‑year‑old Breton woman named Louise Cansot, who was a Paris life model in 1949.

Jaenada’s book seeks not only to uncover the facts of the 1949 murder but also to rehabilitate the reputation of its victim, Louise Cansot, bringing new attention to a case long forgotten.
summary: Philippe Jaenada was announced on Tuesday afternoon as the winner of the Prix Goncourt for his novel L’Inconnue du quai de Javel. The book recreates the 1949 murder of 29‑year‑old Breton life model Louise Cansot and seeks to rehabilitate her reputation.

title: UK food suppliers suffer cyber‑attacks after European freezer temperature hacks
content: Food suppliers in the United Kingdom have experienced cyber‑attacks that followed incidents in which hackers raised the temperatures of supermarket freezers across Europe. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (NSCS) is working with the affected companies, and cybersecurity experts note the national impact is minimal while warning the events could be the “foothills” of a broader threat.
summary: Food suppliers in the UK have been hit by cyber‑attacks after hackers raised the temperatures of supermarket freezers across Europe. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (NSCS) said it is working with the affected companies and that the national impact is minimal.

title: Brazil releases first global roadmap to phase out coal, oil and gas
content:
Brazil has released the world’s first global “roadmap” for phasing out fossil fuels, announcing the plan on Tuesday. The initiative comes from Brazil’s government, which is the host of last year’s UN climate conference and the upcoming COP30 summit.

The roadmap sets out steps to break the link between countries and coal, oil, and gas. It states that nations can begin reducing their fossil‑fuel dependence immediately, without waiting for new technologies or economic shifts. The plan also argues that doing so could boost economies and help lift people out of poverty while moving the focus from negotiating to implementing climate action.
summary: Brazil’s government announced the world’s first global roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels on Tuesday. It says countries can break the link with coal, oil and gas now and could boost economies and pull people out of poverty.

title: Caleb Williams and Jeffery Simmons lead Bears past Seahawks 34-17
content:
The Chicago Bears defeated the host Seattle Seahawks 34-17 on Monday night, powered by an efficient performance from quarterback Caleb Williams and a strong defensive showing by new arrival Jeffery Simmons. Williams completed 71% of his passes for 247 yards without turnovers, throwing a touchdown pass on the opening drive. He was sacked only once against one of the NFL’s stingiest defenses.

On defense, Simmons recorded one sack and six tackles. Running back D’Andre Swift added three rushing touchdowns for the Bears, who improved to a 6-2 record. The Seattle Seahawks have lost three of their last four games.
summary: Caleb Williams threw for 247 yards without turnovers while Jeffery Simmons recorded a sack and six tackles as the Bears defeated the Seahawks 34-17. D'Andre Swift rushed for three touchdowns in the victory over a Seattle team that has lost three of its last four games.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Denzel Bentley Stripped of WBO Title Over Mandatory Challenge Dispute
content:
Middleweight boxer Denzel Bentley has been stripped of his WBO world title after the sanctioning body refused permission for him to defend his belt against Shane Mosley Jr. The WBO rejected Bentley’s appeal last Friday, which argued he was entitled to face the world-ranked Mosley Jr rather than his mandatory challenger in a first title defence. The decision prevents the fight scheduled for this Saturday night at London’s Copper Box Arena.

In an interview at his gym in Essex, Bentley discussed the trauma and street violence that have impacted his life. He revealed that several friends in Battersea were murdered, an experience that numbed him and placed the current boxing politics into perspective. Bentley described his past reluctance to share his story, noting that he has been chased and shot at. Despite the loss of his title and the surrounding political disputes, he remains determined to continue pursuing fights and titles.
summary: Denzel Bentley has been stripped of his WBO world middleweight title after the sanctioning body refused permission for him to defend against Shane Mosley Jr. Bentley stated that he was entitled to face the world-ranked Mosley Jr rather than his mandatory challenger in a first title defence.

title: Point of Law wins 2026 Melbourne Cup after reeling in Royal Supremacy
content:
Point of Law, a three-year-old stallion previously owned by King Charles, won the 2026 Melbourne Cup at Flemington Racecourse. Jockey Ethan Brown guided the Ciaron Maher-trained horse to victory in the $10m feature race, reeling in Royal Supremacy after the rival had led by approximately 20 lengths.

The result marked a significant achievement for trainer Ciaron Maher, who filled the top three places in the event. Point of Law justified his status as the favorite, securing the win in a thrilling finish against his stablemate.
summary: Point of Law, a three-year-old stallion formerly owned by King Charles, won the $10m Melbourne Cup at Flemington Racecourse. Jockey Ethan Brown guided the Ciaron Maher-trained horse to victory after closing on leader Royal Supremacy.

title: West Ham to Appoint Scott Parker After Sacking Nuno Espírito Santo
content:
West Ham are poised to appoint Scott Parker as their manager following the dismissal of Nuno Espírito Santo. Parker, who has been out of work since leaving Burnley last season, is expected to be in place before the club visits Cardiff City on Wednesday.

The sacking comes after West Ham’s 3-1 defeat to West Bromwich Albion last Saturday, which left the side eighth in the Championship. Although the club had retained Nuno, who took over from Graham Potter in September 2025, after their previous Premier League relegation, patience has run out as they aim for an immediate return to the top flight.

title: Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel dies aged 30 after on-pitch collision
content: Forward had cardiac arrest and was taken to hospital He was struck in the chest when challenging for ball The Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel has died following a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a match in Spain’s second division. Tenerife announced that the 30-year-old had tragically passed away at 8am on Tuesday after he had been taken into intensive care on Monday afternoon. De Miguel suffered a cardiorespiratory arrest and did not regain consciousness. The collision occurred in added time at the end of Andorra’s visit to Tenerife, a game that had been put back 24 hours because of the risk of torrential rain on the island. With the score 2-2, late in the 96th minute, a long ball was played away from the Tenerife area and up the pitch. De Miguel chased it into space and Owono came a long way out of his goal, jumping forward and crashing into the attacking player inside the centre circle. Owono was immediately sent off. De Miguel was left unconscious with players from both sides appealing for medical assistance.
summary: Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel died at age 30 after suffering a cardiac arrest following a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono. The incident occurred during a match in Spain’s second division, where Owono was sent off after crashing into De Miguel in the 96th minute.

title: Canada, EU Agree Deeper Cooperation on Energy and Cleantech Supply Chains
content: Canada and the European Union’s commitment to strengthen cooperation on energy security and the energy transition lays the foundation to put clean growth and climate priorities at the heart of their alliance, according to experts. In a seven-page joint statement agreed at the end of a two-day summit in Montreal on Friday, both sides committed to work more closely on investment in critical minerals, green grids, energy sources, battery storage and the protection of energy infrastructure. They agreed to assess opportunities for long-term energy connectivity across the Atlantic, including through a feasibility study on liquefied gas (LNG) exports to Europe. The statement also includes a pledge to “deepen targeted industrial cooperation” on technology value chains and “address bilateral trade barriers”. “Canada and the European Union have sent a clear and unwavering signal that closer cooperation on decarbonisation and climate resilience will be central to their new strategic alliance,” said Canadian Climate Institute president Rick Smith. “The task now is to turn talk into action.” Foundation for climate action The EU and Canada’s “alliance for the future” aims to deepen their partnership across investment, trade and economic security to weather geopolitical tensions and global threats, including “the existential threat of the interdependent crises of climate change, biodiversity loss, ocean and land degradation, and pollution”. These threats are “increasingly impossible to ignore as the impacts of extreme heat, wildfires, floods, and other disasters become more disruptive and expensive,” Smith said. Oct 7, 2026 News New Zealand accused of breaching EU trade deal over climate rollbacks The EU’s climate trade rules face their first major test after a green group alleged New Zealand violated binding environmental provisions under its trade deal with the bloc Oct 28, 2026 News Tensions set to flare over trade at COP31 as China makes it a priority After difficult talks in Belém last year, trade is likely to remain a sticking point at COP31 despite Brazil’s efforts to contain the issue to a series of dialogues Sep 15, 2026 Business International trade linked to 20% of global emissions – but imports ignored Researchers say governments should discuss how to tackle emissions linked to globally traded goods and services, especially in large importing countries The statement reaffirms existing commitments established by the Canada-European Union Green Alliance, which both parties described as “our compass for advancing decarbonisation while also strengthening competitiveness, affordability, and economic security”. Investment in critical minerals During the summit, the European Investment Bank (EIB) announced a “new chapter” for its presence in Canada, beginning with accelerated investment in critical minerals. “At a time when both sides of the Atlantic are working to reduce strategic dependencies, we want to turn our partnership into investment in real projects, from mining and processing to recycling,” EIB Vice-President Nicolas Beer said in a statement. “That is how we build supply chains that are not only more secure, but more competitive too.” Joanna Kyriazis, director of policy and strategy at Clean Energy Canada, welcomed the EIB announcement as a “bright spot of the summit” and “one of the few tangible actions”. “As the EU and Canada seek to advance a partnership anchored in ensuring mutual security and navigating an uncertain world, it is essential that electrification remains a north star… one of the greatest ways we can advance both short- and long-term affordability, competitiveness, and energy security,” she said. Feasibility of Canadian LNG exports to the EU In addition, the agreement calls for a joint long-term feasibility study on LNG exports to Europe, although no immediate investment was announced to support this. A media briefing circulated by climate advocacy groups in advance of the summit had warned that a call for such a study would support Canada’s efforts to rebrand gas, a highly polluting fossil fuel, as a reliable, low-carbon energy source. Yet, the agreement was interpreted by some observers as a Canadian concession following more than a year of rhetoric predicting a boom in Canadian gas exports to the EU and elsewhere. Yet Koç Holding has become a top partner while its oil refiner runs flat out and its climate targets slip “What is clear is that the EU is reducing its gas consumption drastically,” Adrian Hiel, director of the Brussels-based Electrification Alliance, told the Globe and Mail. “The long-term trend is clear and by the middle of the next decade, Europe should be out of the LNG game.” Last year, The Energy Mix and Berlin-based Clean Energy Wire reported on mounting doubts that serious European demand for additional gas supplies would ever materialise after Energy and Natural Resources Minister Tim Hodgson touted LNG exports to Germany in “as little as five years”. Rapprochement on a ‘trade irritant’ In the lead-up to the summit, the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation reported that Canadian iron, steel, fertiliser and aluminium would not be exempt from carbon tariffs under the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), as it moves toward full implementation in 2034. The CBAM is a trade tool designed to protect the continent’s domestic industries from competitors in countries with less stringent carbon controls. Unlike other non-EU members like Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, and the UK, Canada is unlikely to be exempted from the CBAM because there are no plans to link its carbon market to Europe’s. However, at the end of the Montreal summit, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told a press conference they had made progress on finding joint solutions to the issue, which von der Leyen described as a “trade irritant”. Canada’s EU ambassador, Jonathan Wilkinson, formerly the environment and climate minister, said Canada sees it as a problem that the CBAM “did not acknowledge Canadian producers were doing their part to reduce their greenhouse gas footprint by paying an industrial carbon price”. He “confirmed diplomatic talks are heading in the right direction but not resolved”, CBC reported. summary: Canada, EU Agree Deeper Cooperation on Energy and Cleantech Supply Chains.

title: Researchers target prolactin receptors to treat lupus
content: Researchers at the University of California, Riverside, and City of Hope have discovered a new strategy for treating systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The approach focuses on correcting an imbalance in prolactin hormone receptors found on disease‑causing immune cells. By targeting these receptors, the team was able to lower inflammatory molecules and reduce harmful immune cells while leaving normal immune cells intact. This finding offers a potential therapeutic direction for managing lupus‑related kidney damage.
summary: Researchers at the University of California, Riverside, and City of Hope identified a new strategy for treating systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The strategy targets an imbalance in prolactin receptors in disease‑causing immune cells, reducing inflammatory molecules and harmful immune cells while preserving normal counterparts.

title: Hereditary lung and liver disease successfully treated for first time with gene correction
content: Alpha‑1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATM) is a congenital metabolic disorder caused by a genetic defect that leads to the incorrect production of the protective protein alpha‑1 antitrypsin (AAT). The deficiency primarily damages the lungs and the liver, and can result in serious conditions such as pulmonary emphysema, liver fibrosis, or cirrhosis. In particularly severe cases, an organ transplant is the last resort. Currently, no curative treatment is available for this disorder.
summary: Alpha‑1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATM) is a congenital metabolic disorder caused by a genetic defect that results in the protective protein alpha‑1 antitrypsin (AAT) being produced incorrectly. For the first time, the disease has been successfully treated using gene correction, offering a potential cure where previously only organ transplant was an option.

title: Medicare spending rises 5.9% per stay after private equity buys hospices
content:
The study found Medicare spending rose by 5.9% per hospice stay after private equity acquisition compared to similar for-profit hospices that were not acquired.

The increase was mainly due to longer stays; the average length of stay rose by 6.3 days.

The shift appears related to patients who use less daily care, with a significant rise in the share of patients with dementia and a larger share of patients discharged from hospice alive.
summary: Medicare spending rises 5.9% per stay after private equity buys hospices.

title: Study Shows 9 of 10 Older Australians Applying for Aged Care Receive Welfare Payments
content: A new study by researchers at Flinders University and the South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute (SAHMRI) examined the financial circumstances, sources of income and homeownership of more than 920,000 older Australians who applied for aged care between 2010 and 2019. The average age of the cohort was 82. The analysis found that nine in ten older Australians applying for aged care receive social welfare payments. The research provides a large‑scale snapshot of the economic profile of the aging population seeking aged‑care services.
summary: Study Shows 9 of 10 Older Australians Applying for Aged Care Receive Welfare Payments.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Child dies of measles, New York's first measles death in 30 years
content: A child in rural northern New York died after contracting measles, the state’s first death from the disease in 30 years, state officials announced Monday.
summary: A child in rural northern New York died after contracting measles. State officials said it is the state's first measles death in 30 years.
author: Medical Xpress

title: WHO urged to review nitrate drinking water standards amid health risk concerns
content: Dozens of global health and environmental organizations urged the World Health Organization on Tuesday to revise its decades‑old standards for nitrate levels in drinking water. The groups argued that the current guidelines do not reflect recent scientific evidence about potential health risks.
summary: Dozens of global health and environmental organizations called on the World Health Organization to revise decades-old nitrate standards for drinking water. They argue the standards do not reflect recent scientific evidence about potential health risks.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Archaeologists identify psychoactive drugs in Inca sacrificial mummies
content: Archaeologists have conducted toxicological examinations of mummified individuals sacrificed at mountain shrines throughout the Inca Empire. The analyses identified psychoactive substances that the victims ingested prior to their deaths, shedding light on the drugs used in the civilization’s principal sacrificial ritual.
summary: Archaeologists performed toxicological analysis on the mummified remains of people sacrificed at mountain shrines across the Inca Empire. The analysis revealed the psychoactive substances they consumed before their deaths.
author: Phys.org

title: Improved snow model better captures Northeast winter thaws and runoff
content: An improved snow model now better captures winter thaws and runoff in the Northeast. Mountain snow there differs from the western United States because the region’s milder, more humid climate shapes winter conditions. Existing snow models often fail to reflect these distinct differences.
summary: The improved snow model more accurately captures winter thaws and runoff in the Northeast. It reflects the region's milder, more humid mountain climate that differs from the western United States.
author: Phys.org

title: Moth study shows gas inside us could fight wound infections
content: A recent study indicates that a gas naturally produced by the human body could help treat skin and wound infections, potentially offering a new approach alongside conventional antibiotics.
summary: A gas naturally produced by our bodies could help treat skin and wound infections. The study suggests it could be used alongside conventional antibiotics.
author: Phys.org

title: Antarctica's Hidden Microbial Biodiversity Powers Its Ecosystems
content: Antarctica is often pictured as a land of penguins, seals, and whales. Yet most of its scientific marvels lie beneath the surface and can only be seen with a microscope. These unseen microbial communities form the foundation of Antarctic ecosystems, remaining largely invisible to most visitors.
summary: Many people imagine penguins, seals and whales when thinking of Antarctica. Most of Antarctica's scientific wonders are microbial communities that form the foundation of Antarctic ecosystems and remain largely invisible to visitors.
author: Phys.org

title: China Imports Millions of Donkey Hides from Africa Every Year, New Book Traces Drivers
content: A new book, China, Africa and the Market for Donkeys, by China‑Africa trade specialist Lauren Johnston, examines the surge in demand for donkey hides over the past 15 years—an increase the author says has been driven mainly by China. Johnston, who spent several years researching the trade, discusses her findings on the drivers and impact of the African‑to‑China hide market.
summary: Demand for donkey hides has grown exponentially over the past 15 years, mainly driven by China. Lauren Johnston, a specialist on China trade with Africa, spent several years researching the donkey trade and published the book "China, Africa and the Market for Donkeys."
author: Phys.org

title: Monarch butterflies get tiny trackers to help scientists follow their mysterious migration
content: Rebeca Quiñonez-Piñón and other scientists are attaching tiny tracking devices to hundreds of monarch butterflies to identify critical stopover locations. This effort aims to find these resting spots before they disappear, addressing the question Quiñonez-Piñón had as a child about where the insects stop for meals and rest during their North American migrations.
summary: As a child, Rebeca Quiñonez-Piñón wondered where monarch butterflies stop for a meal and a night's rest on their long migrations across North America. Now she and other scientists are attaching tiny tracking devices to hundreds of butterflies to find those critical stopover locations before they disappear.
author: Phys.org

title: Fire losses to U.S. buildings could nearly triple by 2060 without new protections
content:
New research from the University of Colorado Boulder's Cooperative Institute for Research in Environmental Sciences (CIRES) indicates that fire losses to U.S. buildings could nearly triple by 2060 without new protections. The study notes that fires in the U.S. are becoming faster, larger, and more dangerous, while people continue to develop and move into fire-prone regions.

According to the researchers, this increased risk to structures will occur if society does not act on climate change, manage vegetation, or transform how buildings are constructed and adapted to fire. The findings highlight the compounding nature of these factors as they approach midcentury.
summary: Fire losses to U.S. buildings could nearly triple by 2060 without new protections.
author: Phys.org

title: Crow experiments show vocal communication requires extra mental effort
content: Research indicates that for animals capable of vocalization, deciding to emit a sound involves multiple neural processes. These processes include controlling the timing of the sound, its loudness, and pitch, while also adaptively switching between vocalization and other behaviors in response to changing circumstances.
summary: Crow experiments suggest that switching to vocal communication requires extra mental effort. The experiments show that choosing to emit a sound involves controlling timing, loudness, pitch, and switching between vocalizations and other behaviors.
author: Phys.org

title: Columnist James Woodford Challenges Boiling Frog Myth with Backyard Evidence
content: Columnist James Woodford reports discovering evidence in his own backyard that challenges the scientific consensus that the "boiling frog" metaphor is a myth. The popular concept suggests frogs die from slow environmental warming because they fail to notice the change, a claim generally dismissed by science. Woodford’s personal observations, however, appear to support the validity of this long-debated analogy.
summary: The boiling frog metaphor claims frogs die when water heats slowly, but science calls it a myth. Columnist James Woodford says he has found evidence against the myth in his backyard.
author: New Scientist

title: Vibrating mattress and nitric oxide pills boost clearance of Alzheimer's protein
content: A study found that lying on a vibrating mattress for 40 minutes while taking two nitric‑oxide‑releasing pills increased the brain’s clearance of an Alzheimer’s‑related protein. The enhanced removal was observed through the brain’s waste‑disposal system.
summary: Participants lay on a vibrating mattress for 40 minutes while taking two nitric‑oxide‑releasing pills. The treatment increased clearance of an Alzheimer's‑related protein through the brain’s waste‑disposal system.
author: New Scientist

title: USC researchers reverse aging liver cells, cut Alzheimer’s protein in half
content:
USC researchers have discovered that rejuvenating liver cells may protect against Alzheimer’s disease and heart disease.  

In a study with rats, an experimental drug restored aged liver cells, halving the amount of an Alzheimer’s‑linked protein and lowering low‑density lipoprotein cholesterol to levels seen in younger animals. The treatment also reactivated a previously unknown communication system that enables liver cells to clear harmful substances from the bloodstream.
summary: USC researchers found that an experimental drug restored aging liver cells in rats, cutting levels of an Alzheimer’s-linked protein in half and bringing bad cholesterol down to youthful levels. The treatment also revived a previously unknown communication system that helps liver cells remove harmful substances from the bloodstream.
author: Science Daily

title: CERN's LHC Finds Big Bang Matter in Small Collisions
content:
Scientists at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider have reported new evidence that even relatively small atomic collisions can recreate the extraordinary state of matter that existed moments after the Big Bang. The findings suggest that these brief, high‑energy interactions produce quark‑gluon plasma, an exotic substance in which ordinary particles dissolve into their fundamental building blocks.

The quark‑gluon plasma forms at temperatures more than 100,000 times hotter than the center of the Sun, providing a unique laboratory for studying the early universe’s extreme conditions.
summary: Scientists at CERN's Large Hadron Collider have uncovered evidence that small atomic collisions can recreate quark‑gluon plasma, the state of matter that existed shortly after the Big Bang. The plasma reaches temperatures over 100,000 times hotter than the Sun's core, breaking ordinary particles into their fundamental components.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists Discover Loophole That Could Allow Fast-Spinning Black Holes to Split
content: Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart, suggesting that extremely fast‑spinning black holes might divide into two. The finding raises the possibility of an entirely new black hole phenomenon that future telescopes could potentially detect.
summary: Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart. The finding suggests that extremely fast-spinning black holes might divide into two, a new phenomenon that future telescopes could detect.
author: Science Daily

title: Extra weight may be aging your brain faster than you think
content: A 24‑year study of more than 8,200 adults found that excess body weight may accelerate brain aging, leading to faster declines in memory, concentration, and decision‑making skills. The effect was strongest among people over 65, raising concerns about the long‑term effects of obesity on brain health.
summary: A major 24-year study involving more than 8,200 adults suggests that excess body weight may accelerate brain aging, leading to faster declines in memory, concentration, and decision-making skills. The connection was particularly strong among people over 65, raising concerns about the long-term effects of obesity on brain health.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find experimental drug for Alzheimer’s repairs DNA damage, cuts inflammation
content: Scientists discovered that a drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries can address key features of Alzheimer’s disease, including DNA damage and inflammation. The experimental treatment has already undergone initial safety testing in humans and may expedite therapies that target the disease’s root causes.
summary: Scientists discovered that a drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries can address several key features of Alzheimer’s disease, including DNA damage and inflammation. The experimental treatment has already undergone initial safety testing in humans, potentially allowing a faster route to disease‑targeting therapies.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientist Siddhartha Roy wins 2026 Maddox prize after Flint water controversy
content:
A new Guardian podcast features Dr Siddhartha Roy, who was a third‑year PhD student when Flint, Michigan’s water supply was found to contain dangerous levels of lead. Roy was part of a team of scientists that publicly disputed state and federal statements that the water was safe, and his role earned him local recognition as a hero.

The episode recounts how subsequent research questioned the earlier belief that Flint’s children had suffered permanent brain damage. Roy’s commitment to following the evidence, regardless of the reaction it provoked, was cited as the reason he received the 2026 Maddox prize, an award for individuals who defend science and evidence in the face of hostility. In the interview with Ian Sample, Roy reflects on his Flint experience and explains why his work led to the loss of personal friendships.

Listeners can also explore additional Guardian coverage of the Flint water crisis and support the outlet through the provided link.
summary: Scientist Siddhartha Roy wins 2026 Maddox prize after Flint water controversy.
author: Guardian Science

title: 2026 Pacific Northwest sees heightened storm activity and rare annular typhoons
content:
The Pacific’s tropical cyclone activity has remained high since April 2026, when Sinlaku intensified to super typhoon strength and struck Micronesia, Guam, and the Northern Mariana Islands. By the end of October, the Northwest Pacific Basin still hosted active storms. On October 29, 2026, the EPIC camera aboard the DSCOVR satellite captured an image of Super Typhoon In‑fa near the Mariana Islands, while the remnants of Typhoon Champi moved toward Alaska amid a series of storms traversing the Bering Sea. In‑fa was the fifth typhoon to reach the Mariana Islands that year, and the MODIS instrument on NASA’s Terra satellite recorded the storm the following day, just west of the island chain.

In‑fa displayed characteristics of an annular tropical cyclone: a nearly circular shape, a large eye, and an absence of prominent outer rainbands. Annular storms are uncommon, representing only about 4 percent of tropical cyclones in the western North Pacific. Their eyes average roughly 45 kilometers in diameter, larger than the 25‑kilometer eyes typical of standard tropical cyclones, and they tend to maintain strength longer in unfavorable conditions. By the time EPIC captured In‑fa, the storm remained tropical, whereas Champi’s remnants had undergone extratropical transition and entered the Bering Sea’s storm track.

Extratropical cyclones differ from tropical cyclones by having cold cores and drawing energy from temperature contrasts between warm and cold air masses. They usually develop fronts and large comma‑shaped cloud bands. NASA meteorologist Gary Partyka noted that extratropical transitions often expand a storm’s wind field, covering a larger area even if wind speeds do not increase. In this case, Partyka suggested that Champi’s remnants likely intensified a midlatitude system over the Bering Sea, creating a large, comma‑shaped cloud pattern on October 30.

Champi’s transformation followed a destructive path across the West Pacific, where it reached maximum sustained winds of nearly 300 kilometers per hour, prompting some observers to label it one of the season’s strongest storms. The typhoon narrowly missed Taiwan and Guam but delivered damaging winds and heavy rains to those islands, as well as to parts of China and Japan. When its remnants reached Alaska, the state avoided catastrophic damage comparable to the October 2025 impact of ex‑typhoon Halong, though some areas experienced high winds, heavy rain, and snowfall. According to University of Alaska Fairbanks meteorologist Rick Thoman, Champi was the fourth ex‑typhoon to enter Alaskan waters in 2026, following Bang‑Lang, Dujuan, and Choi‑wan. Thoman noted that roughly 60 ex‑typhoons have impacted Alaska since 1970.

Partyka described 2026 as a “particularly active year” for Pacific tropical cyclones, increasing the likelihood that Alaska would be affected by storms that had transitioned extratropically. He cited the strong El Niño underway in the Pacific as a likely contributor to the heightened activity, noting that El Niño tends to steer storms northward toward Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, Japan, and the Korean Peninsula. The Earth Observatory images used in this report were taken by Michala Garrison from DSCOVR EPIC and MODIS data via NASA EOSDIS LANCE and GIBS/Worldview.
summary: 2026 Pacific Northwest sees heightened storm activity and rare annular typhoons.
author: NASA News
